definition_zh: 西红柿；番茄；番茄果实
definition_en: a soft round red fruit with many small seeds, eaten raw in salads or cooked in sauces
core_image: 藤上挂着几颗果皮紧绷的红果，用手一掐就渗出汁水
scene: 夏天傍晚，菜园的木架上爬满了藤，有几颗果实红得发亮。She picked a ripe tomato and ate it warm from the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 tomato 就是「西红柿」这一果实（第 1 个义项：藤上的番茄果实）；句意为她摘下一颗熟透的西红柿，趁还被太阳晒得温热时吃掉了。画面里有菜园木架、藤蔓与红果。

pos.zh: 名词：西红柿；西红柿果实
名词：西红柿植株（园艺用法）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加复数词尾 -es 构成，义为「西红柿（复数）」
口语中加 -ey 构成，义为「带着番茄味与番茄气的」
复合名词，义为「番茄膏；浓缩番茄酱」

senses.title: The red fruit on the vine
senses.definition: the soft red fruit of a plant of the nightshade family, eaten as a vegetable
senses.definitionCN: 茄科植物的柔软红色果实，被当作蔬菜食用
senses.example: She sliced a warm tomato straight from the garden onto the bread.
senses.exampleCN: 她把刚从园里摘下的温热西红柿切成片放在面包上。
senses.why: The word names the plant before it names the fruit, exactly as it did when it arrived from the Americas.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指植株再指果实，与它从美洲传入时的情况一致。

senses.title: The plant that bears the fruit
senses.definition: the bushy plant with hairy stems and yellow flowers that produces tomatoes
senses.definitionCN: 茎上有毛、开黄花、结番茄的灌木状植物
senses.example: The tomatoes along the south wall need staking before the wind rises.
senses.exampleCN: 南墙边的西红柿需要在大风来前绑上支架。
senses.why: Since one plant can carry many fruits, the plural form often names the plants in a garden.
senses.whyCN: 一株能结很多果，所以复数常指园子里的植株。

senses.title: The fruit in cooking
senses.definition: the fruit as an ingredient, used for sauce, soup, or juice
senses.definitionCN: 作为食材的番茄，用于酱汁、汤或果汁
senses.example: Long cooking turns the tomato sweet and thickens the sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间炖煮会让番茄变甜，酱汁也随之变稠。
senses.why: Once processed, the fruit stops being a thing on a plate and becomes a flavour base.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被加工，这颗果就不再是盘中之物，而成了味道的底子。

senses.title: The colour of the fruit
senses.definition: a strong red colour like that of a ripe tomato
senses.definitionCN: 像熟透西红柿那样浓烈的红色
senses.example: The kitchen wall was painted tomato, which made the small room glow.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房墙刷成番茄红，让小房间显得发亮。
senses.why: Bright fruits often give their names to colours, and this one is now a standard paint chip.
senses.whyCN: 鲜艳的果实常把自己的名字借给颜色，如今它已是一个标准的漆色名。

senses.title: The word as a term in biology
senses.definition: in botany, Solanum lycopersicum, whose fruit is classed as a berry
senses.definitionCN: 植物学中指 Solanum lycopersicum，其果实属于浆果
senses.example: Botanists class the tomato as a berry, though cooks treat it as a vegetable.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家把番茄归为浆果，尽管厨师把它当蔬菜。
senses.why: The fruit develops from a single ovary with soft flesh, which is the botanical test for a berry.
senses.whyCN: 这种果由单个子房发育、果肉柔软，正好符合植物学上「浆果」的判断标准。

senses.title: The American pronunciation split
senses.definition: the vowel of the second syllable differs between British and American speech
senses.definitionCN: 第二音节元音在英式与美式发音中不同
senses.example: Visitors from different countries argue about how the tomato should be said.
senses.exampleCN: 来自不同国家的访客会为这个词该怎么读争论。
senses.why: The word travelled into English twice, and the two vowel shapes survive as accents.
senses.whyCN: 这个词两次进入英语，两种元音形态就以口音的形式留了下来。

senses.title: The tomato as a cultural symbol
senses.definition: the fruit as an emblem of long life in some cultures, or of the summer table in others
senses.definitionCN: 在某些文化里象征长寿，在另一些文化里象征夏日餐桌的果实
senses.example: On the painted bowl, a single tomato promises a long and full life.
senses.exampleCN: 在那只彩绘碗上，一颗番茄寓意长寿与丰足。
senses.why: Round red fruits appear in folk decoration where abundance is wished, so the fruit carries meaning beyond food.
senses.whyCN: 圆而红的果实在民间图案里用来祈求丰足，于是它承载了食物之外的意义。

senses.title: The tomato as a household staple
senses.definition: the fruit regarded as an ordinary item of the weekly shopping
senses.definitionCN: 被视为每周采购清单里最普通一员的番茄
senses.example: A bowl of tomatoes sat on the counter beside the bread and the salt.
senses.exampleCN: 一只盛着番茄的碗放在台面上，旁边是面包和盐。
senses.why: As soon as a food is cheap enough to buy weekly, its name becomes an ordinary household word.
senses.whyCN: 当一种食物便宜到可以每周买，它的名字就成了寻常家常用语。

intro.en: The word reached Europe through Spanish from Nahuatl tomatl, the language of central Mexico, and the botanical name added by Linnaeus keeps that origin.
intro.cn: 这个词经西班牙语从墨西哥中部的纳瓦特尔语 tomatl 传入欧洲，林奈所定的学名保留了这个来源。

items.en: The Spanish settlers first used the word for a related green fruit, and early Italian writers called it pomo d'oro, the golden apple.
items.cn: 西班牙殖民者最初用这个词指一种相近的绿色果实，早期意大利作家把它称为 pomo d'oro，即金苹果。

items.en: French travellers borrowed the fruit under Italian names before the Spanish word came north.
items.cn: 法国旅行者先以意大利名称借入这种果实，西班牙语的词形后来才北上。

items.en: English adopts tomato in the seventeenth century, soon after the plant arrives in European gardens.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 tomato，此时这种植物刚进入欧洲花园不久。

items.en: For two centuries the fruit is treated with suspicion by English cooks, who grow it mainly for medicine and ornament.
items.cn: 有两个世纪，英国的厨师对这种果实心存疑虑，主要种来入药与观赏。

items.en: By the nineteenth century tomato sauce and canned tomato make the word an everyday item of the kitchen.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，番茄酱与罐装番茄让这个词成了厨房里的日常用语。

items.en: Linnaeus had already placed the plant in Solanum, and the species name lycopersicum means wolf peach.
items.cn: 林奈早已把这种植物归入茄属，种名 lycopersicum 意为「狼桃」。

note.cn: 形近组收集同属茄科的其他名物，近义组则汇集描述这种果实及其用法的厨房词汇。

normalIntro.en: These memories use the Nahuatl origin, the plural spelling, the compound kitchen phrases, and the British and American vowels.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用纳瓦特尔语来源、复数拼法、厨房复合词以及英美元音差异。

normal.en: The Nahuatl word was tomatl, and the Spanish added a vowel while keeping the stem.
normal.cn: 纳瓦特尔语原词是 tomatl，西班牙语保留了词干并加上了元音。

normal.en: The plural is tomatoes with -es, not tomatos, just as potato makes potatoes.
normal.cn: 复数是 tomatoes，用 -es 而非 -os，和 potato 变 potatoes 一样。

normal.en: Tomato sauce, tomato juice, and tomato soup show the fruit as an ingredient.
normal.cn: tomato sauce、tomato juice、tomato soup 表明这种果可以当食材。

normal.en: Cherry tomato names the small salad variety, and the modifier tells the size.
normal.cn: cherry tomato 指做沙拉的小品种，前面的修饰语说明大小。

normal.en: Britons say a long ah in the middle and Americans a long ay, and both are correct.
normal.cn: 英国人把中间读成长音 ah，美国人读成长音 ay，两种都对。

abstract.en: The word itself travelled from Mexico to Spain to Italy to England, and the fruit followed the same road.

definition_zh: 吨；大量；许多；（船舶的）吨位
definition_en: a unit of weight of about a thousand kilograms, or a very large amount of something
core_image: 吊钩把一大捆钢锭慢慢放上货船的甲板
scene: 港口清晨，吊车把一捆捆钢材放上货轮，甲板被压得吱吱作响。The crane lifted a ton of steel onto the deck in a single swing.
sceneCN: 这里 ton 是重量单位「吨」（第 1 个义项：约一千公斤的重量单位）；句意为吊车一次就把一吨钢吊上甲板。画面里有货轮、吊钩与钢锭。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加复数词尾 -s 构成，义为「许多；大量」
由本词加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「吨位；总吨数」
由本词加 -er 构成的复合成分，义为「……吨级的船或车」

senses.title: The unit of weight
senses.definition: a unit of weight equal to about one thousand kilograms, with several regional variants
senses.definitionCN: 约等于一千公斤的重量单位，各地有不同变体
senses.example: The lorry was carrying fifteen tons of sand.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆卡车装着十五吨沙子。
senses.why: The word is a spelling of tun, the great cask that once set the standard for what a ship could carry.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原是 tun（大酒桶）的拼法，那只大桶曾经规定了船只载重的标准。

senses.title: A very large quantity
senses.definition: an informally large amount of something that is counted by feel rather than by weight
senses.definitionCN: 口语中凭感觉估计的「很多」，而非实际称重
senses.example: I have tons of emails to answer before Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 周五之前我有一大堆邮件要回。
senses.why: Once a ton means a thousand kilos, saying tons becomes the easiest way to say a lot.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一吨意味着上千公斤，说 tons 就成了表示「很多」最省力的方式。

senses.title: The ton as a measure of a ship
senses.definition: a measure of the carrying capacity of a ship by volume rather than by weight
senses.definitionCN: 按容积而非重量衡量船舶载运能力的单位
senses.example: The ship is registered at six thousand tons and carries a crew of thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船登记吨位为六千吨，载有三十名船员。
senses.why: Ships were once rated by how many wine casks they could hold, so the cask became the ship's unit.
senses.whyCN: 船曾按能装多少桶酒来评级，于是那只桶就成了船的单位。

senses.title: A heavy blow or impact
senses.definition: used in phrases to describe a heavy or sudden shock
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语中描述沉重而突然的一击
senses.example: The news hit him like a ton of bricks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息像一记重锤砸在他身上。
senses.why: A ton is a thousand kilos, so anything arriving like a ton of bricks is arriving with enormous weight.
senses.whyCN: 一吨是上千公斤，所以「像一吨砖那样砸下来」就是带着巨大重量到来。

senses.title: The imperial and American variants
senses.definition: the long ton of the British system and the short ton of the American one differ by about a hundred kilograms
senses.definitionCN: 英制长吨与美制短吨相差约一百公斤
senses.example: British lorries are rated in long tons while American freight is listed in short tons.
senses.exampleCN: 英国货车按长吨标定，而美国的货运单用短吨。
senses.why: Two systems inherited the same cask-based unit and then fixed it at different weights, so the spellings and the numbers both diverge.
senses.whyCN: 两套制度继承了同一个源于酒桶的单位，却把它定成不同的重量，于是拼法与数字都出现了分歧。

senses.title: The metric ton
senses.definition: the tonne of a thousand kilograms, now the standard unit in trade and science
senses.definitionCN: 即 tonne，一千公斤，如今是贸易与科学中的标准单位
senses.example: The contract specifies a metric ton, which avoids confusion between the older units.
senses.exampleCN: 合同写明用公吨，以免旧单位之间的混淆。
senses.why: Trade needed one shared figure, and the decimal ton supplied it by dropping the older barrels altogether.
senses.whyCN: 贸易需要一个共通的数字，公吨干脆抛开旧酒桶，正好提供了这个数字。

senses.title: Speed as an informal unit
senses.definition: used in idioms to mean a very fast speed, as in at a ton
senses.definitionCN: 在习语中表示极快的速度，如 at a ton
senses.example: The little motorbike came down the hill at a ton.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆小摩托以极快的速度冲下山坡。
senses.why: A hundred miles an hour was once the top of the scale, and the heaviest unit on hand was borrowed to mean the fastest speed.
senses.whyCN: 一小时一百英里曾是速度的上限，人们就借了手边最重的一个单位来表示最快。

senses.title: A great weight of feeling
senses.definition: the weight of a duty or a sorrow spoken of as if it could be weighed
senses.definitionCN: 把责任或悲伤说得仿佛可以称重
senses.example: He carried a ton of guilt about the missed call.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那个没接的电话背着一吨重的愧疚。
senses.why: Feelings are described with weights all the time, and the heaviest unit makes the metaphor as heavy as it can go.
senses.whyCN: 情感本来就常被说成重量，用最重的单位可以让这个比喻重到极点。

intro.en: The word is the same as tun, the large cask, and its history runs from wine barrels to ship capacity and finally to a plain weight.
intro.cn: 本词与 tun（大酒桶）同形同源，其历史从酒桶到船舶容量，最后落到一个平常的重量单位。

items.en: Late Latin tunna names a cask, probably borrowed from a Celtic word for a container.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 tunna 指酒桶，一般认为借自凯尔特语中表示容器的词。

items.en: Old French tonne keeps the sense of a large barrel and carries it into English.
items.cn: 古法语 tonne 保留大桶之义，并把这一含义带入英语。

items.en: English tun means a large cask, and tunne or ton is used for its capacity as a measure of wine.
items.cn: 中古英语 tun 意为大酒桶，tunne 或 ton 又用来表示桶的容量作为酒的计量。

items.en: A ship's size is stated in tons of cask capacity, which later shifts from volume to weight.
items.cn: 船的规模按「可装多少桶」的吨位陈述，这一用法后来由容积转向重量。

items.en: The weight ton of twenty hundredweight becomes standard in trade, with a British long ton and an American short ton.
items.cn: 二十英担的重量吨成为贸易标准，并分出英国长吨与美国短吨。

items.en: The metric ton of a thousand kilograms is now the international unit, though tons of in speech still just means a lot.
items.cn: 一千公斤的公吨如今是国际单位，而口语里的 tons of 仍然只是「许多」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short words built on the same old cask and the units around it, while the near-meaning group gathers measures of weight and amount.
note.cn: 形近组收集由古酒桶一词以及周边单位构成的短词，近义组则汇集表示重量与数量的词。

normalIntro.en: These memories start from the cask behind the word, then use the unit family and the everyday idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条先从这个词背后的酒桶说起，再利用单位词族与日常习语。

normal.en: The word is tun, the wine cask, spelled with an o when it became a weight.
normal.cn: 这个词就是 tun，那只酒桶，在变成重量单位时改写成 o。

normal.en: Tons of is the spoken phrase for a lot, and the plural is what makes it informal.
normal.cn: tons of 是口语里的「很多」，用复数才显得随意。

normal.en: Tonnage adds -age and names a whole fleet's capacity.
normal.cn: tonnage 加 -age，指整个船队的总容量。

normal.en: A metric ton is a tonne, spelled with the -ne that marks the continental unit.
normal.cn: 公吨写作 tonne，那 -ne 是欧洲大陆单位的标记。

normal.en: A ton of bricks is a phrase about impact, not about construction.
normal.cn: a ton of bricks 说的是撞击，不是建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a crane cable going tight as a dark block of steel clears the dock.

abstract.en: A ton is roughly what a small car weighs, so the word gives a body-sized sense of heaviness.

sensesIntro.en: From one wine cask the entry spreads to a fixed weight, a ship's capacity, informal quantities, and finally to blows and burdens that feel as heavy as a ton.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一只酒桶出发，本词条目扩到固定的重量、船的容量、口语里的数量，最后是像一吨那么重的撞击与负担。

branches.en: Impact and burdens measured by feel.

definition_zh: 音调；语调；语气；色调；腔调；使更有力；健身
definition_en: the quality of a sound or of a voice that shows feeling, or the shade of a colour, or the general character of something
core_image: 一根琴弦被拨动，绷出一声清亮的响，随后慢慢松开
scene: 老师在讲台上停下来，把声音放低，看着最后一排说话的学生。Her tone changed from friendly to formal the moment the noise began.
sceneCN: 这里 tone 是说话时的「语气」（第 2 个义项：语调传达的感情色彩）；句意为喧闹一开始，她的语气就从亲切变得正式。画面里有讲台、安静下来的教室与低下来的声音。

pos.zh: 动词：使（肌肉）结实；使更具力量

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -al 构成，义为「音调的；色调的」
加 -less 构成，义为「单调的；没有感情色彩的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「强身练习；色调处理」
加前缀 in- 与 -ation 构成的名词，义为「语调；声调」

senses.title: The pitch of a musical sound
senses.definition: the height or depth of a sound, measured by the speed of its vibration
senses.definitionCN: 声音的高低，由振动快慢决定
senses.example: The piano tuner tested each tone from the lowest string upward.
senses.exampleCN: 调音师从最低的弦开始，一个音一个音地试。
senses.why: The Greek root tonos means a stretching, as of a string, and a stretched string is what gives a tone its height.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根 tonos 意为「拉紧」，就像绷紧的弦，而绷紧的弦正是音高的来源。

senses.title: The feeling carried by a voice
senses.definition: the quality of a voice that shows the speaker's attitude or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 说话人声音中流露的态度或感情
senses.example: Her tone told us the discussion was over.
senses.exampleCN: 她的语气告诉我们讨论到此为止。
senses.why: A stretched string has tension, and the voice carries a similar tension that listeners hear as attitude.
senses.whyCN: 绷紧的弦有张力，说话的声音也带着类似的张力，听者会把它听成态度。

senses.title: A shade of colour
senses.definition: a particular shade of a colour, or the general brightness of a picture
senses.definitionCN: 颜色的某一种深浅，或画面的整体明暗
senses.example: The walls were painted in warm tones of cream and sand.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁被漆成奶油色与沙色这类暖色调。
senses.why: Painters speak of a picture's tonality, the overall balance of light and dark, and that language passed from music to colour.
senses.whyCN: 画家讲一幅画的「色调关系」即整体明暗平衡，这套说法是从音乐借到颜色上的。

senses.title: The spirit of a place or event
senses.definition: the general character or mood that something has
senses.definitionCN: 某事物整体的性质或气氛
senses.example: The chairman's opening remarks set the tone for the whole meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 主席的开场白为整场会议定下了基调。
senses.why: A gathering has a pitch of feeling the way a string has a pitch of sound, so the musical word shifts to mood.
senses.whyCN: 一场聚会的情感有音高，正如弦有音高，于是音乐用语转到了气氛上。

senses.title: Firmness of muscle
senses.definition: the healthy firmness of a muscle or of skin
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉或皮肤健康而有弹性的状态
senses.example: Regular swimming gave her arms a healthy tone.
senses.exampleCN: 经常游泳让她的手臂结实而有弹性。
senses.why: A muscle in good condition is under steady tension, the same tightness the Greek root named.
senses.whyCN: 状态良好的肌肉保持着稳定的张力，正是那个希腊词根所说的紧绷。

senses.title: To make something firmer
senses.definition: to make a muscle firmer, or to make a body more supple
senses.definitionCN: 使肌肉更结实，或使身体更柔韧
senses.example: Gentle exercises tone the back without straining it.
senses.exampleCN: 轻柔的运动能锻炼背部而不使其拉伤。
senses.why: The verb is formed directly from the noun of firmness, so the action is simply to produce that firmness.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词直接由表示结实的名词构成，动作就是产生那种结实。

senses.title: A difference of pitch in language
senses.definition: in some languages, a difference of pitch that changes the meaning of a word
senses.definitionCN: 在某些语言中，音高差别会改变词义的声调
senses.example: In that language the same syllable in a rising tone means a different thing entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 在那门语言里，同一个音节用升调就完全是另一个意思。
senses.why: Language uses the same small differences of pitch that music does, so a single word covers both systems.
senses.whyCN: 语言利用的正是音乐里那种微小的音高差别，于是一个词同时覆盖两套系统。

senses.title: To soften or moderate
senses.definition: to make a statement, colour, or sound less strong
senses.definitionCN: 使说法、颜色或声音变得不那么强烈
senses.example: The editor asked him to tone down the last paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑请他缓和一下最后一段的措辞。
senses.why: Turning a sound or a statement down lowers its pitch and volume, and the particle turns that image into a verb phrase.
senses.whyCN: 把声音或说法调低，就是降低它的音高与音量，这个小词把这一意象变成了动词短语。

senses.title: A telephone signal
senses.definition: the sound heard in a telephone receiver that shows the line is free or busy
senses.definitionCN: 从听筒中听到的声音，表示线路空闲或占线
senses.example: She lifted the receiver and waited for the dial tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她拿起听筒，等着拨号音。
senses.why: The steady hum of a free line is a single sustained pitch kept at one height, exactly what a tone is.
senses.whyCN: 空闲线路里那声平稳的嗡鸣就是一个保持在同一高度的持续音，正合 tone 之本义。

intro.en: Tone comes from Latin tonus, a stretching or tension, which in turn borrowed Greek tonos, and the musical sense grew out of the image of a tightened string.
intro.cn: tone 来自拉丁语 tonus（拉紧、张力），后者借自希腊语 tonos；音乐含义正是从「绷紧的弦」这一意象长出来的。

items.en: Tonos means a stretching or tightening, used of a bowstring, a rope, and later of the voice.
items.cn: 希腊语 tonos 意为拉紧、绷紧，用于弓弦、绳索，后来也用于嗓音。

items.en: Latin tonus keeps both the physical sense of tension and the musical sense of pitch.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tonus 同时保留「张力」的物理意义与「音高」的音乐意义。

items.en: Old French ton carries the word into the Romance speech of the Middle Ages with the sense of a musical sound.
items.cn: 古法语 ton 把这个词带入中世纪的罗曼语，含义为乐音。

items.en: English borrows tone in the thirteenth century for a musical note or the pitch of a voice.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 tone，指乐音或嗓音的音高。

items.en: By the eighteenth century tone extends to colours and to the mood of a gathering.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，tone 扩展到颜色与聚会的氛围。

items.en: The verb to tone, meaning to give firmness, appears later, and with down and up it becomes an everyday phrase.
items.cn: 表示「使之结实」的动词 tone 出现较晚，与 down、up 搭配后成了日常短语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects derivatives of the same stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for sound quality and for mood.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干的派生词，近义组则汇集表示音质与气氛的词。

normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「绷紧的弦」这一词根、与 up 和 down 构成的动词短语，以及颜色义项入手。

normal.en: Tone of voice is the phrase to keep when the sense is attitude.

normal.en: Set the tone means fixing the mood at the outset, and the verb makes it an act.

normal.en: Tone down lowers intensity, while tone up raises firmness, and the particle tells you which.

normal.cn: tonal 与 toneless 把词族分成「有声调」与「无声调」两路。

abstract.en: Picture a singer holding one note until the air in the room seems to stand still.
abstract.cn: 想象一位歌手拖住一个音，直到室内的空气仿佛静止。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp turned down one notch, and the whole room becomes a softer shade.
abstract.cn: 想一盏灯被调低一档，整个房间随之变成更柔的色调。

abstract.en: A voice can be a hand: soft on the shoulder, or flat on the table.
abstract.cn: 声音可以像一只手：轻轻搭在肩上，或重重拍在桌上。

examples.cn: 他用平静的语气回答。

examples.en: The curtains are a light tone that makes the room look larger.
examples.cn: 窗帘是浅色调，让房间显得更大。

examples.en: She swims twice a week to tone her arms.
examples.cn: 她每周游两次泳来锻炼手臂线条。

definition_zh: 表土；土壤剖面最上部富含有机质的一层
definition_en: the upper, darker and more fertile layer of soil, where roots and organic matter are concentrated
core_image: 苗床边一车深褐色松软的土被摊平，铁锹划过时留下湿润的土纹
scene: 花坛边上，园艺工把一车深褐色的松软土倒在苗床上，用铁锹摊平，说 A good topsoil holds moisture without turning to mud after rain.
sceneCN: 这里 topsoil 指「剖面最上部富含有机质的那层土」，取第 1 个义项（表土层本身）；句意为好的表土能保住水分，雨后又不会变成烂泥。图中可辨识物件：苗床、土堆、铁锹、土纹。

pos.zh: 表土（多作不可数，指具体土类时可用复数 topsoils）

derivatives.zh: 各类表土（复数，用于土壤调查比较）
表层施肥；在表面铺一层土或肥料
底土、心土
土壤；弄脏

senses.title: The fertile surface layer
senses.definition: the upper layer of soil, darker and richer in organic matter than what lies beneath
senses.definitionCN: 土壤的上部层，比下面的土颜色更深、有机质更多
senses.example: Most of the field's fertility sits in the topsoil.
senses.exampleCN: 这块田的肥力大部分集中在表土里。
senses.why: Top marks the upper position and soil names the material, so the compound simply says which layer is meant.
senses.whyCN: top 标出上部位置，soil 指明材料，因此这个复合词只是说明所指是哪一层。

senses.title: The plough layer
senses.definition: the part of the topsoil that tillage mixes and crops are sown into
senses.definitionCN: 被耕作搅动、作物播种其中的那部分表土
senses.example: Deep ploughing buries weed seeds below the plough layer of topsoil.
senses.exampleCN: 深耕把杂草种子埋到耕作层下面。
senses.why: Farming measures the layer by the depth of the plough, so the word often means the worked slice rather than the whole surface.
senses.whyCN: 农业以犁的深度来计量这一层，因此这个词常指被翻动的那一片，而不是整个表层。

senses.title: Bought soil for gardens
senses.definition: bagged or delivered soil sold for beds, lawns and planters
senses.definitionCN: 装袋或送货上门、用于花坛、草坪与种植箱的土壤
senses.example: The new border was filled with imported topsoil.
senses.exampleCN: 新花境是用外购表土填起来的。
senses.why: Once gardens were built on subsoil or rubble, suppliers began selling the good upper layer as a product with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 当花园建在底土或碎砖上时，供应商开始把优质的上层土当作商品出售，这个词也就成了商品名。

senses.title: Stripping before construction
senses.definition: the practice of removing and stockpiling the surface layer before building or mining
senses.definitionCN: 在施工或采矿前把表层土取走并堆存的做法
senses.example: Topsoil stripping was required before the foundations were dug.
senses.exampleCN: 开挖基础之前必须先剥离表土。
senses.why: Because the layer is slow to form, regulations require it to be saved and put back rather than buried.
senses.whyCN: 由于这一层形成极慢，法规要求把它保存下来再回填，而不是直接埋掉。

senses.title: Loss through erosion
senses.definition: the removal of the fertile layer by water or wind, leaving poorer ground behind
senses.definitionCN: 肥沃表层被水或风带走，留下更贫瘠的地面
senses.example: Topsoil loss on the slope doubled after the hedges were cleared.
senses.exampleCN: 树篱被清除后，坡地上的表土流失翻了一倍。
senses.why: The layer is the first thing moving water meets, so it is lost before anything deeper is touched.
senses.whyCN: 这一层是流水最先碰到的东西，因此在更深处被动到之前它就已被带走。

senses.title: Where roots and seeds live
senses.titleCN: 根系与种子最密集的一层
senses.definition: the zone holding most fine roots, soil animals and the seed bank
senses.definitionCN: 容纳大部分细根、土壤动物与种子库的那一层
senses.example: Almost every fine root in the meadow was inside the topsoil.
senses.exampleCN: 草甸里几乎每一条细根都在表土之内。
senses.why: Air, water and organic matter all peak near the surface, so life concentrates there by necessity.
senses.whyCN: 空气、水与有机质都在近地表处最充足，因此生命必然集中在那里。

senses.title: Replacement in restoration
senses.definition: the return of stored surface soil after mining or construction so that vegetation can recover
senses.definitionCN: 采矿或施工结束后把堆存的表土回填，使植被得以恢复
senses.example: Topsoil replacement gave the restored slope a chance to green again.
senses.exampleCN: 表土回填让修复后的坡面有了重新变绿的机会。
senses.why: Stored soil keeps its seeds and microbes, which is why returning it is cheaper than rebuilding fertility.
senses.whyCN: 堆存的土保有种子与微生物，因此回填比重新造肥力更省事。

senses.title: Disturbed urban surface soil
senses.definition: the mixed, compacted surface layer of cities, often part rubble and part imported soil
senses.definitionCN: 城市里被混合、压实的表层，常一半是碎砖一半是外运来的土
senses.example: Urban topsoil often drains badly because it has been compacted for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 城市表土常因被压实几十年而排水很差。
senses.why: City soils are made by digging and filling rather than by slow formation, so the word marks position rather than quality.
senses.whyCN: 城市土壤由挖填而成，而非缓慢生成，因此这个词在这里标出的是位置而不是质量。

intro.en: Topsoil is an English compound of top, from Old English topp, a tuft or summit, and soil, from Old French soil and Latin solum. The agricultural compound is recorded from the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: topsoil 是英语复合词，由 top 与 soil 组成：top 来自古英语 topp「一簇、顶端」，soil 来自古法语 soil 与拉丁 solum。这个农业复合词在十九世纪已有书证。

items.en: Topp meant a tuft of hair or the summit of something, and top kept the idea of the highest position.
items.cn: topp 意为一撮毛发或某物的顶端，top 保留了「最高位置」的意思。

items.en: Soil came through Old French from Latin solum, ground or sole, so the second half names the material rather than a place.
items.cn: soil 经古法语来自拉丁 solum「地面、脚底」，因此后半部分命名的是材料而非地点。

items.en: Nineteenth-century farming and soil survey needed to separate the fertile surface from the poorer layer beneath, and topsoil supplied that contrast with subsoil.
items.cn: 十九世纪的农业与土壤调查需要把肥沃表层与下面较贫瘠的层分开，topsoil 与 subsoil 正好提供这对区分。

items.en: Twentieth-century construction and mining added stripping and replacement, treating the layer as a resource to be moved and stored.
items.cn: 二十世纪的施工与采矿增加了剥离与回填的用法，把这一层当作可搬运、可储存的资源。

items.en: The compound is written as one word in technical use and is uncountable except when soil types are compared.
items.cn: 这个复合词在技术文献中写作一个词，除比较土类外通常不可数。

note.en: Group one holds the layer words that sit beside topsoil in any description; group two holds materials often sold or spread like topsoil.
note.cn: 第一组是任何描述中都会与表土并列的层位词；第二组是常被当作表土出售或铺撒的材料。

entries.definition: The layer beneath the topsoil, usually poorer in organic matter and richer in clay.
entries.definitionCN: 表土之下的层，通常有机质更少、黏土更多。

entries.definition: The general word for the plant-growing layer; topsoil names only its upper part.
entries.definitionCN: 指能生长植物的土层的统称；topsoil 只指它的上部。

entries.definition: The highest part of anything; on its own it says nothing about soil.
entries.definitionCN: 任何事物的最高部分；单独使用时与土壤无关。

entries.definition: Material lying above a coal seam or ore body; it includes topsoil but is defined by what lies beneath.
entries.definitionCN: 压在煤层或矿体之上的材料；它包含表土，但以所覆盖之物来定义。

entries.definition: A descriptive phrase for the uppermost soil, common in survey writing without the agricultural overtone.
entries.definitionCN: 对最上部土壤的描述性说法，常见于土壤调查文献，不带农业色彩。

entries.definition: The depth actually turned by the plough, which may be thinner than the whole topsoil.
entries.definitionCN: 犁实际翻到的深度，可能比整个表土层薄。

entries.definition: A balanced mix of sand, silt and clay; a topsoil can be loam, but loam is not a position.
entries.definitionCN: 砂、粉砂与黏土的均衡混合；表土可以是壤土，但壤土不是位置。

entries.definition: Decomposed organic waste used as a soil amendment; it is added to topsoil rather than being it.
entries.definitionCN: 腐解的有机废弃物，用作土壤改良剂；它是加进表土的东西，而不是表土本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Old English top word and the real topsoil-subsoil pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的古英语 top 词与真实的表土—底土成对关系。

normal.en: Top plus soil: the soil at the top, which is exactly what the word says.
normal.cn: top 加 soil：最上面的那层土，词面说的就是这意思。

normal.en: Topsoil and subsoil come as a pair, like roof and cellar.
normal.cn: 表土与底土成对出现，就像屋顶与地窖。

normal.en: Most roots, seeds and organic matter sit in the topsoil.
normal.cn: 大部分根、种子与有机质都在表土里。

normal.en: Construction language adds stripping and replacement of topsoil.
normal.cn: 施工语境里还有表土剥离与表土回填的说法。

normal.en: Topsoil loss is the first damage reported after land is cleared.
normal.cn: 土地被清理后，最先报告的破坏就是表土流失。

abstract.en: Picture a thin dark blanket over pale ground, and everything alive living inside that blanket.
abstract.cn: 想象浅色地面上盖着一条深色薄毯，所有活物都住在毯子里。

abstract.en: Picture a bulldozer pushing the good layer into a heap to keep it for later.
abstract.cn: 想象推土机把好土推成一堆，留着以后再用。

abstract.en: Picture rain carrying the dark blanket downhill and leaving stones behind.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水把那层深色毯子冲下山坡，只留下石头。

examples.en: The topsoil here is only a few centimetres deep.
examples.cn: 这里的表土只有几厘米深。

examples.en: Builders must strip and store the topsoil before grading the site.
examples.cn: 施工方在平整场地前必须剥离并堆存表土。

examples.en: Adding compost improved the topsoil within two seasons.
examples.cn: 加入堆肥后，表土在两个季节内就改善了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「头顶那层土」——top 是顶，soil 是土，最上面那层肥沃的土就是表土

root: top（古英语 topp「顶端、一簇」）+ soil（古法语 soil「一块地」，上溯拉丁 solum「地面」）；「位于最上部的土壤」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the layer itself to the worked slice, the bagged product, stripping, erosion, the root zone, restoration and the disturbed city surface.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从这一层本身走到被耕作的切片、袋装商品、剥离、侵蚀、根区、复垦，以及受扰动的城市表层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark crumbly layer spread over a pale bed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层深色松软的土铺在浅色苗床上。

branches.en: POSITION AND WORK: the layer at the top, and the slice a plough actually turns.
branches.cn: 位置与作业：位于顶部的那层，以及犁实际翻到的那一片。

branches.en: COMMERCE: good surface soil becomes a bagged product for gardens.
branches.cn: 买卖：优质表层土变成花园用的袋装商品。

branches.en: MOVING IT: stripped before building, put back after mining.
branches.cn: 搬运：施工前剥离，采矿后回填。

branches.en: LOSING IT: water and wind take the layer first.
branches.cn: 失去它：水与风最先带走这一层。

branches.en: LIFE AND CITY: the root zone, and the compacted urban version of the same layer.
branches.cn: 生命与城市：根区，以及同一层在城市里被压实后的样子。

intro.en: Topsoil joins two free morphemes, top and soil, and both halves also appear in other compounds.
intro.cn: topsoil 由 top 与 soil 两个自由语素组成，两半也出现在其他复合词中。

latinIntro.en: Top is native English, while soil reaches Latin solum through French. The Latin entry below records only that second half.
latinIntro.cn: top 是英语本族词，soil 则经法语上溯拉丁 solum。下面的拉丁词条只记录后半部分。

items.structure: top (Old English topp, tuft or summit)
items.example: The top of the slope dries out first.
items.exampleCN: 坡顶最先变干。

items.structure: soil (Old French soil, a plot of land)
items.example: The soil here is thin and stony.
items.exampleCN: 这里的土薄而多石。

items.example: Topsoil was saved in a heap beside the site.
items.exampleCN: 表土被堆存在工地旁边。

items.example: The survey compared topsoils across the valley.
items.exampleCN: 调查比较了谷地各处的表土。

items.meaning: the layer beneath the surface soil
items.example: Subsoil showed up as soon as the pit deepened.
items.exampleCN: 坑一挖深，底土就露出来了。

items.example: A light topdressing evened out the lawn.
items.exampleCN: 轻轻铺一层表土把草坪找平了。

items.example: The topmost layer is the darkest.
items.exampleCN: 最上面一层颜色最深。

items.example: Litter is a soil-forming input.
items.exampleCN: 枯落物是成土的输入之一。

latinEntries.example: The soil in topsoil is this Latin noun, worn down through French.
latinEntries.exampleCN: topsoil 中的 soil 就是经法语磨损后的这个拉丁名词。

definition_zh: 龙卷风；陆龙卷；（旧义）雷暴；旋风般的一阵
definition_en: a violently rotating column of air extending from a thundercloud to the ground
core_image: 漏斗状的黑云从雷暴底部垂到地面，所过之处尘土、木板与树枝被卷上天
scene: 警报器在镇上响起，人们抱着孩子跑向地下室，广播员喊道 A tornado touched down in the wheat field west of town.
sceneCN: 这里 tornado 指「从雷暴云伸到地面的旋转空气柱」（第 1 个义项：气象学意义上的陆龙卷）；句意为一个龙卷风在镇子西边的小麦田里触地。

pos.zh: 龙卷风；陆龙卷；旋风般的一阵

collocations.zh: 龙卷风警报（已发现龙卷风）
龙卷风警戒（条件可能形成）

derivatives.zh: 龙卷风的；具有龙卷风特征的
龙卷风生成
龙卷风般的
防龙卷风的
易发龙卷风的

senses.title: Rotating column touching the ground
senses.titleCN: 陆龙卷：触地的旋转空气柱
senses.definition: a violently rotating column of air in contact with both a thundercloud and the ground
senses.definitionCN: 同时接触雷暴云与地面的猛烈旋转空气柱
senses.example: The tornado flattened two barns in less than a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 龙卷风不到一分钟就推平了两座谷仓。
senses.why: The meteorological definition turns on ground contact: a funnel that never touches down is not counted as one.
senses.whyCN: 气象学定义的关键在是否触地：始终没触地的漏斗云不算龙卷风。

senses.title: Any violent whirlwind
senses.definition: in everyday speech, any destructive whirling wind, whatever its origin
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中泛指任何破坏性的旋转风，不论其成因
senses.example: A tornado of dust crossed the road and blinded the drivers.
senses.exampleCN: 一团尘土旋风横过公路，让司机们看不见路。
senses.why: Ordinary speakers name the visible violence rather than the classification, so the word widens beyond the technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 普通人按可见的暴力命名，而不按分类，因此这个词超出技术义。

senses.title: Old sense: a thunderstorm
senses.definition: in sixteenth- and seventeenth-century English, a violent thunderstorm rather than a funnel
senses.definitionCN: 在 16 与 17 世纪英语中，指猛烈的雷暴而非漏斗云
senses.example: In the old chronicle a tornado broke the masts of three ships.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部旧编年史里，一场雷暴折断了三艘船的桅杆。
senses.why: The word came from Spanish for a thunderstorm; the modern funnel sense narrowed from that wider weather event much later.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自西班牙语中「雷暴」的说法；现代漏斗义是后来从这一更宽的天气事件收窄出来的。

senses.title: West African squall line
senses.titleCN: 西非常见用法：飑线雷暴
senses.definition: in West African English, a line of violent thunderstorms with sudden cool wind
senses.definitionCN: 西非英语中指伴随骤起凉风的强雷暴线
senses.example: The harmattan tornado rolled in from the savannah at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时，来自稀树草原的雷暴飑线滚滚而来。
senses.why: Regional usage kept the older broad sense, so the same word names a thunder line on another continent.
senses.whyCN: 地域用法保留了较早的宽泛义，因此同一个词在另一块大陆指雷暴线。

senses.title: The disaster event
senses.titleCN: 作为灾害事件的龙卷风
senses.definition: the storm viewed as an event that destroys buildings and takes lives
senses.definitionCN: 从摧毁建筑、夺走生命的灾害事件角度看的龙卷风
senses.example: The tornado killed eleven people on the edge of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这场龙卷风在城市边缘夺走了十一条生命。
senses.why: Reports and insurance claims treat the vortex as a single catastrophic event, and the word follows that usage.
senses.whyCN: 报道与保险理赔把涡旋当作单一灾难点，这个词也随之这样用。

senses.title: Figurative burst
senses.definition: a sudden overwhelming burst of applause, criticism or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 掌声、批评或情绪突然而压倒性的一阵爆发
senses.example: A tornado of applause met the singer at the end of the song.
senses.exampleCN: 歌曲结束时，一阵暴风般的掌声迎向歌手。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the shape: something arrives spinning, fast, and sweeps everything up.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了形状：某物旋转着快速到来，把一切卷起。

senses.title: Tornado season
senses.definition: the spring period in which tornadoes are most frequent in a region
senses.definitionCN: 某地区龙卷风最频繁的春季时段
senses.example: The plains grow quiet again after tornado season ends.
senses.exampleCN: 龙卷风季结束后，平原又安静下来。
senses.why: The season is named for its dominant hazard, a common pattern in weather vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 季节以主导灾害命名，这是天气词汇常见的模式。

senses.title: The aircraft name
senses.definition: a twin-engine combat aircraft produced in Europe, known by the proper name Tornado
senses.definitionCN: 欧洲联合研制的双发战斗机，以专名 Tornado（狂风）称呼
senses.example: The Tornado flew low over the valley on a training sortie.
senses.exampleCN: 狂风战斗机在一次训练飞行中低空掠过山谷。
senses.why: Weapon names borrow the force of natural phenomena, so the storm word becomes a proper name for a machine.
senses.whyCN: 武器命名借用自然现象的威力，因此风暴词成了机器的专名。

intro.en: Tornado is a blend of two Spanish weather words: tronada 'thunderstorm', from tronar 'to thunder', and tornado 'turned, rotating', from tornar 'to turn'. English borrowed it as a word for a thunderstorm and only later narrowed it to the funnel.
intro.cn: tornado 由两个西班牙语天气词混合而成：tronada「雷暴」（来自 tronar「打雷」）与 tornado「旋转的」（来自 tornar「转」）。英语借入时指雷暴，后来才收窄为漏斗云。

items.en: Latin tonare 'to thunder', with the noun tonitrus 'thunder', supplied the first half of the Spanish word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tonare「打雷」及其名词 tonitrus「雷」提供了西班牙语词的前半部分。

items.en: Spanish tronada meant 'thunderstorm', built on tronar 'to thunder'; it named the whole storm, not a funnel.
items.cn: 西班牙语 tronada 意为「雷暴」，由 tronar「打雷」构成；它指整场风暴，而非漏斗。

items.en: Separately, tornar 'to turn' (from Latin tornare) produced tornado 'turned, rotating'; English speakers blended the two Spanish forms.
items.cn: 另一方面，tornar「转」（来自拉丁 tornare）构成 tornado「旋转的」；英语使用者把两个西班牙语形式混合起来。

items.en: Early English records use tornado for a violent thunderstorm at sea, especially in accounts of the Caribbean and the Atlantic.
items.cn: 早期英语记载用 tornado 指海上猛烈的雷暴，尤见于加勒比与大西洋的记述。

items.en: The narrow funnel sense established itself in the nineteenth century, once observers began requiring contact with the ground.
items.cn: 狭窄的漏斗义在 19 世纪确立，因为观测者开始要求它必须触地。

note.en: The first group looks similar in spelling but comes from other roots; the second group holds the rotating-wind family and its synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组拼写相近但词根不同；第二组是旋转风家族及其同义词。

entries.definition: From Latin torpedo 'numbness, the numb fish'; it names a underwater weapon, with no turning or thunder in its root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 torpedo「麻木、电鱼」；指水下武器，词根里没有转或雷。

entries.definition: From Spanish torear 'to fight bulls', from toro 'bull'; the ending -dor marks an agent, not a storm.
entries.definitionCN: 来自西班牙语 torear「斗牛」，源于 toro「公牛」；词尾 -dor 表施事者，不是风暴。

entries.definition: The past participle of tear 'to rip'; it looks close but belongs to a completely different verb.
entries.definitionCN: tear「撕」的过去分词；形近但属于完全不同的动词。

entries.definition: From Latin torrens 'rushing, burning', from torrere 'to scorch'; it names a fast stream, not a wind.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 torrens「奔流、灼烧」，源于 torrere「烤焦」；指急流，不是风。

entries.definition: A general term for a rapidly rotating mass of air, often smaller and less organised than a tornado.
entries.definitionCN: 快速旋转气团的通称，通常比龙卷风更小、更有组织性更弱。

entries.definition: A large low-pressure system with rotating winds, hundreds of times wider than a tornado.
entries.definitionCN: 带旋转风的大型低压系统，宽度可达龙卷风的数百倍。

entries.definition: A tropical storm of the Atlantic with sustained winds above 119 km/h; a different scale of phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 大西洋持续风速超过每小时 119 公里的热带风暴；现象尺度不同。

entries.definition: An informal American word for a tornado, used mostly in news headlines and speech.
entries.definitionCN: 美式口语中对龙卷风的说法，多用于新闻标题与口语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Spanish blend, real meteorological terms and the real compound family, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：西班牙语混合来源、真实气象术语与真实复合词族，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: tronada 'thunderstorm' plus tornado 'turned': a storm that turns.
normal.cn: tronada「雷暴」加 tornado「旋转的」：一场会转的风暴。

normal.en: The same thunder root sits in detonate and tonitrus.
normal.cn: 同一个「雷」词根在 detonate 与 tonitrus 里。

normal.en: Warning means it has been seen; watch means it might form.
normal.cn: warning 表示已经发现；watch 表示可能形成。

normal.en: Tornado alley is the plains strip where they are most frequent.
normal.cn: tornado alley 是龙卷风最频繁的平原狭长地带。

normal.en: The plural is usually tornadoes, sometimes tornados.
normal.cn: 复数通常写 tornadoes，有时写 tornados。

abstract.en: Picture a black funnel stitching the cloud to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一个黑色漏斗把云和地面缝在一起。

abstract.en: Picture straw driven into a wooden post by the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一根稻草被风钉进木柱。

abstract.en: Picture applause arriving like weather through a theatre.
abstract.cn: 想象掌声像天气一样扫过剧场。

examples.en: A tornado watch was issued for the whole county by noon.
examples.cn: 到中午时，整个县都发布了龙卷风警戒。

examples.en: The tornado lifted a truck and dropped it in the next field.
examples.cn: 龙卷风把一辆卡车卷起，又把它扔到隔壁田里。

examples.en: Meteorologists count a funnel as a tornado only when it touches the ground.
examples.cn: 气象学家只有在漏斗云触地时才把它算作龙卷风。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陀螺转」——像陀螺一样贴地狂转的风

root: 西班牙语 tronada「雷暴」（tronar「打雷」，拉丁 tonare「打雷」）与 tornado「旋转的」（tornar「转」，拉丁 tornare「转」）混合而成。英语 17 世纪借入时指海上雷暴，19 世纪才专指触地的漏斗云；词源清楚，义项收窄的年代有明确记载。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one funnel: the technical vortex, the everyday whirlwind, the old thunderstorm sense, the West African squall, the disaster, the metaphor, the season and the aircraft name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个漏斗展开：技术涡旋、日常旋风、旧雷暴义、西非飑线、灾害事件、比喻义、龙卷风季与飞机专名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark funnel hanging from a thundercloud and stirring dust at the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑色漏斗从雷暴云垂下，在地面搅起尘土。

branches.en: TECHNICAL AND EVERYDAY: one strict definition with ground contact, one loose name for any visible whirl.
branches.cn: 技术与日常：一个是要求触地的严格定义，一个是任何可见旋风的宽泛叫法。

branches.en: TWO OLD WEATHER SENSES: the English thunderstorm of the seventeenth century and the West African squall line keep the wider meaning.
branches.cn: 两个旧的天气义：17 世纪英语的雷暴与西非的飑线保留了更宽的含义。

branches.en: DISASTER AND CALENDAR: the event that destroys and the season that schedules it.
branches.cn: 灾害与日历：造成破坏的事件与为它排定时间的季节。

branches.en: SOCIAL BURST: applause and criticism can arrive with the same spin.
branches.cn: 社会爆发：掌声与批评能以同样的旋转到来。

branches.en: NAME REUSED: the storm word becomes a proper name for a combat aircraft.
branches.cn: 名称再用：风暴词成为战斗机的专名。

intro.en: Tornado has no English prefix or suffix; it is a borrowed Spanish blend. Its derivatives are compounds and the learned adjective tornadic.
intro.cn: tornado 没有英语前缀或后缀；它是借入的西班牙语混合词。其派生形式是复合词与学术形容词 tornadic。

latinIntro.en: Two Latin families meet in this word: tonare 'to thunder' and tornare 'to turn'. Both are genuine and both are visible in the Spanish forms.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词里汇合了两个拉丁词族：tonare「打雷」与 tornare「转」。两者都真实存在，且都能在西班牙语形式中看到。

items.structure: Spanish tronar 'to thunder', from Latin tonare
items.example: Spanish tronar 'to thunder' is the source of tronada, the older word for a storm.
items.exampleCN: 西班牙语 tronar「打雷」是 tronada（较早的风暴说法）的来源。

items.structure: Spanish tornar 'to turn', from Latin tornare
items.example: Spanish tornar 'to turn' gives tornado its rotating sense.
items.exampleCN: 西班牙语 tornar「转」赋予 tornado 旋转的含义。

items.example: The ending makes tornado literally 'turned'.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使 tornado 字面上就是「被转动的」。

items.example: Tornadic winds are the strongest on the Plains.
items.exampleCN: 龙卷风风力是平原上最强的。

items.example: Tornadogenesis began along the dry line.
items.exampleCN: 龙卷风生成在干线一带开始。

items.example: A tornado-like vortex formed over the lake.
items.exampleCN: 湖面上形成了一个龙卷风般的涡旋。

items.example: The shelter is tornado-proof.
items.exampleCN: 这个避难所是防龙卷风的。

items.example: The county is tornado-prone in spring.
items.exampleCN: 这个县春季易受龙卷风袭击。

definition_zh: 折磨；酷刑；拷打；极度痛苦；使受折磨
definition_en: the act of causing severe pain to punish or force a confession, or great mental suffering
core_image: 绳索被绞紧，一具身体在绳子另一端绷得笔直
scene: 牙科诊室外的长椅上，患者捏着挂号单，听见里面机器的声音就皱起眉。Waiting three hours for a reply was pure torture.
sceneCN: 这里 torture 是精神上的「折磨」（第 2 个义项：极度的痛苦煎熬）；句意为等回信的三个小时简直是纯粹的折磨。画面里有诊室外的长椅、捏紧的单子与紧锁的眉。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「受折磨的；（文体）矫揉的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「施酷刑者」
加 -ous 构成，义为「折磨人的；曲折痛苦的」
同根形容词，义为「曲折的；拐弯抹角的」

senses.title: The deliberate infliction of pain
senses.definition: the act of causing severe physical pain to a person, often to punish or to extract information
senses.definitionCN: 为使某人受罚或招供而故意造成剧烈肉体痛苦的行为
senses.example: The treaty forbids torture under any circumstances.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约禁止在任何情况下使用酷刑。
senses.why: The legal sense is the oldest one in English, and international law still uses the word in exactly this way.
senses.whyCN: 这个法律义项是英语里最早出现的，国际法至今仍按这一含义使用该词。

senses.title: Severe mental suffering
senses.definition: great suffering of the mind, caused by worry, guilt, or waiting
senses.definitionCN: 由忧虑、内疚或等待造成的巨大精神痛苦
senses.example: The weeks before the results came out were torture for the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 结果公布前的几周对全家都是折磨。
senses.why: Pain that is not physical still feels inflicted, so the old word for bodily torment moves into the mind.
senses.whyCN: 非身体的痛苦仍像是被人施加的，于是那个老旧的肉体折磨之词转入了心灵。

senses.title: Something that causes suffering
senses.definition: a thing or situation that is extremely unpleasant to endure
senses.definitionCN: 极难忍受的事物或处境
senses.example: That traffic on Friday evenings is absolute torture.
senses.exampleCN: 周五傍晚的那段交通简直是折磨。
senses.why: Everyday things that cannot be escaped often take the strongest available word, and this is one of the strongest.
senses.whyCN: 无法逃避的日常之事常借用手上最强的词，而这正是一个很强的词。

senses.title: To cause pain to someone
senses.definition: to inflict pain on a person, physically or mentally
senses.definitionCN: 在肉体或精神上给某人造成痛苦
senses.example: He was tortured by doubt for months before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 决定之前，他被疑虑折磨了好几个月。
senses.why: The verb allows both a physical agent and an abstract one, which is why doubt can torture a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词既可接实在的施动者，也可接抽象者，所以「疑虑」也能折磨一个人。

senses.title: To twist the meaning of words
senses.definition: to force a word or idea into a sense it does not naturally carry
senses.definitionCN: 把一个词或观念硬扭成它本来没有的意思
senses.example: Do not torture the sentence into meaning the opposite of what it says.
senses.exampleCN: 不要把这个句子曲解成与它原意相反的意思。
senses.why: Meaning can be bent out of shape as a body can, which brings the word back to its twisting root.
senses.whyCN: 意义可以像身体一样被扭得变形，这又把这个词带回它「扭」的词根。

senses.title: The historical instrument of law
senses.definition: the use of pain as a legal instrument in past legal systems
senses.definitionCN: 过去法律体系中把疼痛当作法律手段的做法
senses.example: Records show that torture was used to obtain confessions in that court.
senses.exampleCN: 档案显示那个法庭曾用刑讯逼取口供。
senses.why: In legal history the word names an admitted procedure, which is what makes it valuable in reading old records.
senses.whyCN: 在法律史上这个词曾指一种被承认的程序，读旧档案时正因如此才需要它。

senses.title: The writer's strained style
senses.definition: in the phrase tortured style, language that is forced and unnatural
senses.definitionCN: 在 tortured style 这一说法中，指勉强而不自然的文笔
senses.example: The translation reads in a tortured style that hides the plain sense.
senses.exampleCN: 这份译文文笔矫揉，把明白的意思藏了起来。
senses.why: Style that is forced is like a rope pulled too far, so the same adjective serves both pain and prose.
senses.whyCN: 强扭的文风就像拉得太过的绳，于是同一个形容词兼用于痛苦与文笔。

senses.title: The metaphor of the twisted rope
senses.definition: the underlying image of something twisted out of its natural shape
senses.definitionCN: 底层意象是某物被扭离其自然形态
senses.example: The road tortures itself around the mountain through a dozen hairpins.
senses.exampleCN: 那条路绕山拐了十几个急弯。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical image in the background, while the adjective tortuous shows it plainly.
senses.whyCN: 名词把物理意象留在背景里，而形容词 tortuous 把它明明白白地呈现出来。

intro.en: Torture comes from Latin tortura, a twisting, from torquere, to twist; the sense moved from bending the body out of shape to pain inflicted on purpose.
intro.cn: torture 来自拉丁语 tortura（扭绞），源于 torquere（扭）；其义从把身体扭得变形，转到故意施加的痛苦。

items.en: Torquere means to twist or bend, and tortura is a twisting, used of ropes under strain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 torquere 意为扭、弯，tortura 是扭绞本身，用于受力的绳索。

items.en: In legal Latin tortura names the application of force to make a person speak.
items.cn: 在法律拉丁语中，tortura 指施加暴力以逼人开口。

items.en: Old French torture carries the legal sense of judicial tormentation into medieval courts.
items.cn: 古法语 torture 把司法拷问的法律含义带入中世纪法庭。

items.en: English borrows torture in the fifteenth century, first as a legal term and then more widely.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 torture，先作为法律术语，后扩展到更广的用法。

items.en: The mental sense, as in the torture of waiting, becomes common in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 「等待的折磨」这类精神意义在十八世纪普遍起来。

items.en: The older physical image survives in tortuous, the adjective for a winding road, and in the mechanics of torque.
items.cn: 古老的物理意象保存在 tortuous（形容蜿蜒之路）与力学中的 torque 里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the twisting-root relatives, while the near-meaning group gathers words for suffering and for cruelty.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一「扭绞」词根的亲属词，近义组则汇集表示痛苦与残暴的词。

normalIntro.en: These memories use the twisting root shared with torque and tortuous, the two senses of body and mind, and the phrase be tortured by.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用与 torque、tortuous 共有的「扭绞」词根、身心两个义项，以及 be tortured by 这一搭配。

normal.en: The root is twist, so torture is a body or a mind twisted out of its shape.
normal.cn: 词根是「扭」，所以折磨就是把身体或心思扭得变形。

normal.en: Torture, torque, and tortuous share the twist, and their meanings tell you which way it went.
normal.cn: torture、torque、tortuous 共用「扭」，各自的含义说明它扭向了哪边。

normal.en: Be tortured by doubt is the common passive pattern for the mental sense.
normal.cn: be tortured by doubt 是精神义常用的被动态。

normal.en: Sheer torture and mental torture both take the noun as an uncountable mass.
normal.cn: sheer torture 与 mental torture 都把名词当作不可数的整体。

normal.en: Tortured style means forced writing, which is the same twist applied to language.
normal.cn: tortured style 指矫揉的文笔，就是把同样的扭力施加到语言上。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled tight until it hums, and then pulled further.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳被拉紧到发出嗡声，然后又被拉。

abstract.en: Think of a clock face you cannot stop watching while you wait for news.
abstract.cn: 想一张你等消息时无法不看的钟面。

abstract.en: Torture is imposed pain, and the word keeps the memory that it was once done with ropes.
abstract.cn: 酷刑是被施加的痛，这个词保存着它曾用绳索实施的记忆。

examples.en: The prisoners were held for weeks without charges or torture of any kind.
examples.cn: 这些被拘留者数周未受指控，也没有遭受任何形式的酷刑。

examples.en: He was tortured by the memory of what he had said.
examples.cn: 他被自己所说过的话的记忆折磨着。

examples.en: The long bus ride was torture for the children.
examples.cn: 漫长的长途汽车之旅对孩子们是种折磨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「同扯」——两人同扯一根绳，扯得生疼，就是折磨。

root: 拉丁语 torquere（扭、绞）→ tortura（扭绞；刑讯）→ 古法语 torture → 英语 torture。同根词有 torque、tortuous、tort。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the deliberate infliction of pain, then moves to the suffering that is not physical, to the verb of tormenting, and at last back to the twisting image that started it: twisted words, twisted roads, and twisted style.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从故意施加的痛苦写起，再到非身体的苦痛、表示折磨的动词，最后回到最初的「扭」这一意象：扭曲的词、蜿蜒的路与矫揉的文风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something pulled or twisted out of its natural shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：被拉扯、扭离其自然形态之物。

branches.en: Pain inflicted deliberately, by law or by force.
branches.cn: 由法律或暴力故意施加的痛苦。

branches.en: Suffering of the mind and the things that cause it.
branches.cn: 精神苦痛及其来源。

branches.en: The verb of tormenting or being tormented.
branches.cn: 折磨或被折磨的动词用法。

branches.en: Meaning and style twisted out of shape.
branches.cn: 被扭曲的意义与文风。

branches.en: The rope image carried into roads and mechanics.
branches.cn: 绳索意象被带入道路与力学。

intro.en: The word comes from a Latin twisting stem with -ura, and English adds -ed, -er, -ous, and the parallel -uous.
intro.cn: 本词由拉丁语「扭绞」词干加 -ura 构成，英语再加 -ed、-er、-ous 以及平行的 -uous。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the twisting verb, its noun, and the related noun for torment.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出「扭绞」动词、其名词以及相关的「苦痛」名词。

items.example: The stem is the twisted body of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干是这个词被扭过的主体。

items.example: Tortura is the act of twisting.
items.exampleCN: tortura 是扭绞这一行为。

items.example: Tortured means having been tortured.
items.exampleCN: tortured 意为受过折磨的。

items.example: Torturer names the one who acts.
items.exampleCN: torturer 指施加者。

items.example: Torturous means full of torture.
items.exampleCN: torturous 意为充满折磨。

items.example: Tortuous means full of twists.
items.exampleCN: tortuous 意为曲折多弯。

items.example: Torque keeps the physical sense.
items.exampleCN: torque 保留物理意义。

items.example: Tort is the legal cousin of the word.
items.exampleCN: tort 是本词的法律亲属。

items.example: Torment is the sister noun of suffering.
items.exampleCN: torment 是表示苦痛的姊妹名词。

definition_zh: 总的；总计的；完全的；全部；总数；合计达
definition_en: the whole amount of something, or complete and entire, or to add up to a figure
core_image: 一长串账单被最后一道横线压住，末尾写着一个整整齐齐的数
scene: 结账时收银条一路打印到纸尾，最下面那一行加粗。The total for the trip came to more than we had planned.
sceneCN: 这里 total 是「总数、总额」（第 4 个义项：所有部分相加之和）；句意为这趟旅行的总额超出了我们的计划。画面里有长条小票、最末那行加粗的数字。

pos.zh: 形容词：总的；全部的；完全的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成，义为「完全地；全部地」
加 -ity 构成，义为「整体；全部」
加前缀 sub- 构成，义为「小计；部分合计」
由 total 派生的政治术语，义为「极权的」

senses.title: The whole amount
senses.definition: the complete amount obtained by adding all the parts together
senses.definitionCN: 把所有部分相加所得的完整数量
senses.example: The total of the two bills was surprisingly small.
senses.exampleCN: 两张账单的总额小得令人意外。
senses.why: The Latin word for the whole is the direct source, so the noun names the sum in its completeness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「整体」的词是直接来源，故名词指完整加总后的量。

senses.title: Adding up to a figure
senses.definition: to amount to a particular figure when all parts are counted
senses.definitionCN: 各部分组成加总起来达到某个数字
senses.example: The costs totalled more than three thousand yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 这些花费合计超过三千元。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: to make a total out of scattered items.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：把零散的项加总成一个总数。

senses.title: Complete and absolute
senses.definition: used of something with no part missing or no exception allowed
senses.definitionCN: 用于毫无缺失或毫无例外的情形
senses.example: The room fell into total silence when she began to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 她开口时，屋子里一片死寂。
senses.why: If a total is everything, then a total silence is silence without one sound left out.
senses.whyCN: 既然总数意味着全部，那么 total silence 就是一点声音也没遗漏的静。

senses.title: A sum of money owed
senses.definition: the full sum due for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 为货物或服务应付的全部款项
senses.example: Please pay the total within seven days of the invoice.
senses.exampleCN: 请在开票后七天内付清总额。
senses.why: Shops print the total at the bottom of a receipt, since it is the last and whole figure.
senses.whyCN: 商店把小票底部的那个数叫作 total，因为它是最后也是完整的那个数。

senses.title: Counting everything in
senses.definition: including every member or part, as in the total number of students
senses.definitionCN: 包括每个成员或每个部分，如学生总人数
senses.example: The total number of students rose by two hundred this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年学生总人数增加了两百。
senses.why: The adjective marks a count that leaves nothing outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记一种不把任何东西留在外面的计数。

senses.title: A whole in philosophy
senses.definition: in older philosophical writing, the whole made of parts that hang together
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的哲学文字中，指由相联部分构成的整体
senses.example: The old textbook speaks of the total as more than the sum of its parts.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧教材说整体大于其各部分之和。
senses.why: Philosophy uses the word for any whole that holds together, which is the root idea unextended.
senses.whyCN: 哲学用这个词指任何自成一体的整体，这正是未加引申的词根本义。

senses.title: Complete ruin in expressions
senses.definition: used in phrases such as a total loss to mean damage beyond recovery
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a total loss 等短语，表示彻底损失、无法挽回
senses.example: The storm left the boat a total loss.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴使那条船彻底报废。
senses.why: Insurance language needs a word for damage with nothing left to save, and total supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 保险用语需要一个词表示无可挽回的损毁，total 正好提供。

senses.title: Everything considered
senses.definition: used in phrases like in total or a total of to introduce a final count
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in total 或 a total of 等短语引出最终计数
senses.example: A total of forty people signed the sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 共有四十人在表上签了字。
senses.why: The phrase works like a bracket around a list, closing it with one figure.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语像一对括号把一串项目包起来，再用一个数字收尾。

intro.en: Total comes from medieval Latin totalis, an adjective from totus, the Latin word for whole or entire, and it entered English through French.
intro.cn: total 来自中世纪拉丁语 totalis，是 totus（意为「整个、全部」）的形容词，经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Totus means all, whole, or entire, and it has no parts to be counted separately.
items.cn: 拉丁语 totus 意为「全部、整个」，它本身不再被拆成可数的部分。

items.en: The derived adjective totalis names what belongs to the whole rather than to a part.
items.cn: 由它派生的形容词 totalis 指属于整体而非属于部分的。

items.en: Old French takes total as an adjective of the schools and of accounts.
items.cn: 古法语把 total 用作学校与账目中的形容词。

items.en: Middle English borrows the adjective and soon uses it as a noun for the sum.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个形容词，很快又把它用作表示总和的名称。

items.en: The verb to total appears in the eighteenth century in bookkeeping and in arithmetic.
items.cn: 动词 total 于十八世纪出现在簿记与算术中。

items.en: The emphatic sense of complete, as in total silence, spreads in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 表示「完全」的强调义（如 total silence）在十九、二十世纪扩散开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the same stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for sums and for completeness.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干的形式，近义组则汇集表示总和与完整性的词。

normalIntro.en: These memories use the fixed phrases in total and a total of, the bookkeeping verb, and the emphatic use with abstract nouns.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用 in total 与 a total of 的固定搭配、簿记中的动词用法，以及与抽象名词连用时的强调用法。

normal.en: In total and a total of both close a list with one figure.
normal.cn: in total 与 a total of 都用同一个数字为一串项目收尾。

normal.en: A total loss is insurance language, and it means nothing can be saved.
normal.cn: a total loss 是保险用语，意思是无可挽救。

normal.en: The verb is written totalled in British spelling and totaled in American spelling.
normal.cn: 动词在英式拼写中写作 totalled，美式写作 totaled。

normal.en: Total silence means no sound at all, which shows how the word moves from sums to absolutes.
normal.cn: total silence 指一点声音也没有，这显示该词如何从加总走向绝对。

normal.en: Subtotal takes the prefix sub- and gives the sum below the main one.
normal.cn: subtotal 加前缀 sub-，给出主总额之下的那个小计。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures and a single line ruled under the last of them.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字，最后一行下面划着一道横线。

abstract.en: Think of an empty room where even the echo has stopped.
abstract.cn: 想一间空房，连回声都停了。

abstract.en: A total leaves nothing outside it, whether it counts money or measures silence.
abstract.cn: 总数不把任何东西留在外面，无论它数的是钱，还是衡量的是静。

examples.en: In total, the project took eleven months to finish.
examples.cn: 这个项目总共用了十一个月才完成。

examples.en: He was in total agreement with the plan.
examples.cn: 他完全同意这个计划。

examples.en: The company's sales totalled nearly two million units last year.
examples.cn: 去年公司的销量合计接近两百万台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「头托」——把所有数一起托到头上，就是总数 total。

root: 拉丁语 totus（全部、整个）→ 中世纪拉丁语 totalis → 古法语 total → 英语 total。同族词有 totality、subtotal；totus 还与 totidem（同样多）同源。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the added-up sum, then follows the same whole into the verbs of counting, the adjective of completeness, and the emphatic phrases of absolute loss or silence.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从加总求和开始，再沿「整体」这一概念走入计数的动词、表示完整的形容词，以及「彻底损失」「彻底寂静」这类强调短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole closed by a ruled line.
core.cn: 核心意象：被一道横线封住的整体。

branches.en: The sum itself and the phrases that present it.
branches.cn: 总和本身以及呈现它的短语。

branches.en: The act of adding parts into a figure.
branches.cn: 把各部分加成一个数字的动作。

branches.en: Completeness and the total count.
branches.cn: 完整性与全部计数。

branches.en: The philosophical whole.
branches.cn: 哲学意义上的整体。

branches.en: Total loss as damage with nothing left.
branches.cn: 彻底损失指无可挽回的损毁。

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective used as noun, verb, and adjective; its family comes from -ly, -ity, and the prefix sub-.
intro.cn: 本词是兼作名词、动词与形容词的拉丁源形容词，其词族来自 -ly、-ity 与前缀 sub-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give totus and the words formed beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出 totus 及其旁生的词。

items.exampleCN: totalis 给了英语的拼写。

items.example: Totality is the state of being whole.

items.example: A subtotal is a sum below the main one.
items.exampleCN: subtotal 是主总额之下的小计。

items.example: Totalled is the bookkeeping form.
items.exampleCN: totalled 是簿记中的形式。

items.example: Totalling the column took a minute.
items.exampleCN: 把那一列加总用了一分钟。

definition_zh: 触摸；接触；触觉；少量；联系；感动；涉及
definition_en: to put a hand or an object lightly against something, or the act and sense of such contact
core_image: 指尖轻轻碰到冰凉的玻璃，只留下一圈几乎看不见的雾
scene: 展厅里隔着护栏，讲解员举起手示意不许靠近。Please do not touch the paintings on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 touch 是动词「触摸、碰」（第 1 个义项：用手或物体轻触某物）；句意为请不要触摸墙上的画。画面里有护栏、伸出的手与墙上的画框。

pos.zh: 动词：触摸；碰到；感动；涉及
名词：触摸；触觉；少量；联系

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「动人的；感人的」
加 -ed 构成，义为「感动的；有点疯的（口语）」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「未触动过的；未受影响的」
拉丁同源形容词，义为「触觉的」

senses.title: To put a hand on something
senses.definition: to put a hand or finger on something, especially lightly
senses.definitionCN: 用手或手指轻放在某物上，尤指轻轻地
senses.example: She touched the cold glass to feel where the crack began.
senses.exampleCN: 她摸着冰凉的玻璃，想找出裂纹从何处开始。
senses.why: The French verb tocher gave English a word for the light contact of one thing on another.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 tocher 为英语提供了表示一物与另一物轻触的词。

senses.title: An act of contact
senses.definition: the state or act of two things being in contact
senses.definitionCN: 两物相互接触的状态或动作
senses.example: A single touch of the wire set off the alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 电线被碰了一下，警报就响了。
senses.why: The verb and the noun are the same idea seen from two sides, one as action and one as event.
senses.whyCN: 动词与名词是同一概念的两面，一为动作，一为事件。

senses.title: The sense of feeling
senses.definition: the ability of the skin to feel what comes against it
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤感知接触物的能力
senses.example: After the accident he lost the touch in two fingers.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后他两根手指失去了触觉。
senses.why: Among the five senses, touch is the one that works only by direct contact, which is why the word names it.
senses.whyCN: 五官之中，触觉是唯一靠直接接触起作用的，这个词正因此用来命名它。

senses.title: A small amount
senses.definition: a very small quantity of something, often added to a dish or a colour
senses.definitionCN: 极少的一点，常指添进菜肴或颜色的部分
senses.example: Add a touch of salt to the soup before serving.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前在汤里加一点盐。
senses.why: A small amount is like a fingertip of something, just enough to be felt but not taken in bulk.
senses.whyCN: 少量就像指尖沾到的那一点，感觉得到，却谈不上分量。

senses.title: Contact between people
senses.definition: the state of communicating with someone, as in keep in touch
senses.definitionCN: 与人保持交流的状态，如 keep in touch
senses.example: We stayed in touch after we left the same school.
senses.exampleCN: 离开同一所学校后我们一直保持联系。
senses.why: People who correspond are in contact even at a distance, so the physical word carries over to communication.
senses.whyCN: 保持来往的人即便相隔也处于「接触」中，于是物理的词被挪用到交流上。

senses.title: To move someone deeply
senses.definition: to cause a strong feeling of sympathy or gratitude
senses.definitionCN: 引起强烈的同情或感激之情
senses.example: The letter from her old teacher touched her more than any gift.
senses.exampleCN: 老教师的那封信比任何礼物都让她感动。
senses.why: A feeling is said to reach the heart as a hand reaches the skin, so being moved is being touched.
senses.whyCN: 情感像手触到皮肤那样抵达心里，所以被感动就是被 touch 到。

senses.title: To deal with a subject
senses.definition: to mention or deal with a matter briefly
senses.definitionCN: 简短地提到或处理某个问题
senses.example: The report touches on housing but says little about cost.
senses.exampleCN: 报告谈及住房，却很少提到成本。
senses.why: To touch a subject is to come into contact with it lightly, without taking it up fully.
senses.whyCN: touch 一个话题就是轻轻碰到它，并不把它完全展开。

senses.title: A slight trace of a quality
senses.definition: a slight trace of a quality, as in a touch of sadness
senses.definitionCN: 某种特质的一丝痕迹，如 a touch of sadness
senses.example: There was a touch of frost on the windows this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今早窗上有一层薄霜。
senses.why: The sense of a small quantity extends from food to weather and to mood, wherever a trace can be noticed.
senses.whyCN: 「少量」义从食物扩展到天气与心情，凡是能察觉出痕迹的地方都能用。

senses.title: Skill with the hands
senses.definition: a special skill in handling something, as in the common touch or a fine touch
senses.definitionCN: 处理某物时的特别本领，如 the common touch 或 a fine touch
senses.example: The old cook still had a fine touch with pastry.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老厨子做起酥点来仍然手法精到。
senses.why: Skill shows in how the hand meets the material, so a good worker is said to have a good touch.
senses.whyCN: 手艺体现在手与材料相接的方式上，所以好手艺被说成有好的 touch。

senses.title: In football and rugby
senses.definition: in rugby and some other games, the area at the side of the field, or the act of grounding the ball
senses.definitionCN: 在橄榄球等运动中指场边区域，或把球触地的动作
senses.example: The ball went into touch and the line-out followed.
senses.exampleCN: 球出了边线，随后进行边线掷球。
senses.why: The sporting use keeps the literal sense: the ball leaves the field by touching the boundary.
senses.whyCN: 体育用法保留了字面义：球碰到边线而离开场地。

intro.en: Touch comes from Old French tochier, from a Vulgar Latin verb built on a root meaning to knock or strike, and it has been used for both contact and feeling since the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: touch 来自古法语 tochier，其源是表示「敲、击」词根的通俗拉丁语动词；自中世纪以来既指接触，也指感受。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin verb related to toccare means to knock or strike lightly against something.
items.cn: 与 toccare 相关的通俗拉丁语动词意为轻敲或轻击某物。

items.en: Old French tochier carries the senses of touching, tasting, and trying.
items.cn: 古法语 tochier 兼有触摸、品尝与尝试诸义。

items.en: Middle English touchen appears in the thirteenth century for physical contact.
items.cn: 中古英语 touchen 在十三世纪出现，表示身体上的接触。

items.en: The sense of moving the feelings is recorded early, since the heart was thought to be struck by emotion.
items.cn: 「感动」义很早就有了，因为当时认为情感会击中心。

items.en: The phrase keep in touch grows out of the older idea of hands meeting in greeting.
items.cn: keep in touch 这一说法源自更早的「以手相握致意」的想法。

items.en: Touch screens and touch typing make the word name any contact used to give a command.
items.cn: 触摸屏与盲打让这个词指任何用来下达指令的接触。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivative and compound forms, while the near-meaning group gathers verbs for contact and for feeling.
note.cn: 形近组收集派生与复合形式，近义组则汇集表示接触与感受的动词。

affected with gratitude or sympathy
not touched or not affected
entries.definitionCN: 未被触碰的；未受影响的

entries.definition: a burning light carried in the hand
entries.definitionCN: 火把；手电，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to sense by touching or in the mind
the state of touching or communicating
to move a hand gently along something
to cause a strong feeling in someone

normalIntro.en: These memories use the fixed phrase in touch, the quantity sense with of, and the way a physical verb grows into a word for feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用 in touch 的固定说法、a touch of 的数量用法，以及一个物理动词长成情感词的路径。

normal.en: Keep in touch is about writing and calling, not about hands.
normal.cn: keep in touch 说的是写信打电话，与手无关。

normal.en: A touch of salt and a touch of frost both mean a very small amount.
normal.cn: a touch of salt 与 a touch of frost 都指极少的一点。

normal.en: Touch on a subject means to mention it lightly, never to treat it fully.
normal.cn: touch on a subject 指轻轻提到，从不彻底处理。

normal.en: In rugby, the ball goes into touch when it crosses the side line.
normal.cn: 在橄榄球中，球越过边线就叫出 touch。

normal.en: The adjective touching keeps the feeling sense: a touching story moves you.
normal.cn: 形容词 touching 保留感受义：a touching story 让你感动。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip on cold glass and the faint print it leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖按在冰凉的玻璃上，留下淡淡的印。

abstract.en: Think of two wires just meeting, and the whole machine starting up.
abstract.cn: 想两根线刚刚接上，整台机器就启动了。

abstract.en: One light contact is enough to carry either information or feeling.
abstract.cn: 轻轻一次接触，就足以传递信息，也足以传递情感。

examples.en: Do not touch the wet paint on the bench.
examples.cn: 别碰长椅上还没干的油漆。

examples.en: We lost touch for years and then met again at a wedding.
examples.cn: 我们失联多年，后来在一场婚礼上重逢。

examples.en: Her speech touched everyone in the hall.
examples.cn: 她的演讲感动了礼堂里的每一个人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踏实」——手指一碰到就踏实了，能碰到才算真。

root: 通俗拉丁语 toccare（轻敲）→ 古法语 tochier → 中古英语 touchen → 现代 touch。同族词有 touching、untouched；拉丁词根亦见 tactile「触觉的」。

sensesIntro.en: The entry starts from the light contact of the hand, then takes in the sense of feeling, a small amount, human contact, being moved, and finally the technical uses in talk and in sport.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从手的轻触写起，再收进触觉、少量、人际往来、感动，最后是谈话与体育中的专门用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip meeting a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖与表面相接。

branches.en: Contact, the act of contact, and the sense that reads it.
branches.cn: 接触、接触的动作与读取它的触觉。

branches.en: A small quantity and a trace of a quality.
branches.cn: 少量与某种特质的一丝痕迹。

branches.en: Keeping in touch and touching on a subject.
branches.cn: 保持联系与谈及某个话题。

branches.en: Being moved by feeling.
branches.cn: 被情感所动。

branches.en: Skill of hand, and the touch line in sport.
branches.cn: 手上的技巧与体育中的边线。

intro.cn: 本词是兼作名词的借入动词，其词族靠 -ing、-ed、un- 以及与 screen、down 等合成扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the root of knocking and its tactile relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出「敲击」词根及其触觉相关的同族词。
