items.exampleCN: 这个词干来自古法语。

items.example: Toccare underlies the Romance forms.
items.exampleCN: toccare 是罗曼语诸形式的基础。

items.example: Tochier is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: tochier 是直接来源。

items.example: Touching means moving.
items.exampleCN: touching 意为动人的。

items.example: Touched means affected.
items.exampleCN: touched 意为受感动的。

items.example: Untouched means not touched.
items.exampleCN: untouched 意为未被触碰的。

items.example: Touchable surfaces can be handled.
items.exampleCN: touchable 的表面可以触摸。

items.example: A touch screen needs a finger.
items.exampleCN: 触摸屏需要手指操作。

items.example: A touch down is worth five points.
items.exampleCN: 一次触地得分值五分。

definition_zh: 坚韧的；难对付的；艰难的；强硬的；粗暴的；硬汉
definition_en: strong and not easily broken, torn, or defeated; also difficult to deal with or to bear
core_image: 一块旧皮带被反复拉扯，纹路皱起却始终不断
scene: 面试失败第三次，他回家的路上忽然笑了一下。That was a tough year, but it taught me a lot.
sceneCN: 这里 tough 是「艰难的、难熬的」（第 3 个义项：难以应付或难以忍受）；句意为那是艰难的一年，但让我学到了很多。画面里有雨后的街道、走回家的人影。

pos.zh: 形容词：坚韧的；艰难的；强硬的；粗暴的
动词（口语）：坚持；挺过（常与 out 连用）

derivatives.zh: 加 -ness 构成，义为「坚韧；强硬」
加 -ly 构成，义为「强硬地；艰难地」
加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「使变坚韧；使变强硬」
加 -ie 构成，口语义为「难题；难对付的人」

senses.title: Strong and hard to break
senses.definition: strong enough to bend or wear without breaking
senses.definitionCN: 强度足以弯曲磨损而不断裂
senses.example: The old fishing line was still tough after twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这根旧钓线过了二十年依然结实。
senses.why: The Old English word describes what can bear force without giving way, and that physical strength is the base of every other sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词描述能受力而不屈服之物，这份物理上的强韧是其他一切含义的基础。

senses.title: Hard to chew
senses.definition: of food, difficult to cut or chew
senses.definitionCN: 指食物难切难嚼
senses.example: The meat was tough and took an hour to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这肉很老，吃了一个小时才吃完。
senses.why: If a material resists force, then a piece of meat that resists the teeth is tough in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 材料若抗得住外力，那块抗得住牙齿的肉也就同样被称作 tough。

senses.title: Difficult to bear
senses.definition: hard to endure or to live through
senses.definitionCN: 难以忍受或难以度过
senses.example: It was a tough winter with no work and little money.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个没有工作又缺钱的难熬冬天。
senses.why: A hard period strains a person the way force strains a material, so the physical word takes on the sense of hardship.
senses.whyCN: 艰难的日子像外力拉扯材料那样拉扯着人，于是物理词带上了艰苦之义。

senses.title: Requiring effort
senses.definition: needing much effort or skill to deal with
senses.definitionCN: 需要很多努力或技巧才能处理
senses.example: The last question was the toughest one on the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一道题是卷子上最难的一道。
senses.why: A task that resists solution is like a material that resists force, and tough comes to mean difficult.
senses.whyCN: 难解的任务如抗力的材料，于是 tough 被用来表示困难。

senses.title: Severe and firm
senses.definition: firm and severe in dealing with people or crime
senses.definitionCN: 对待人或犯罪时坚定而严厉
senses.example: The city took a tough line on illegal parking.
senses.exampleCN: 该市对违章停车采取了强硬立场。
senses.why: A firm policy does not bend under pressure, which is the physical sense applied to rules.
senses.whyCN: 坚定的政策在压力下不弯，正是物理义用在规则上。

senses.title: Rough in manner
senses.definition: violent or rough in behaviour, often of a neighbourhood or a group
senses.definitionCN: 行为凶悍粗野，常用于街区或人群
senses.example: He grew up in a tough part of town and learned to walk fast.
senses.exampleCN: 他在城里凶悍的街区长大，学会了走路快。
senses.why: A place where one must be strong to survive is called tough, transferring the quality of the person to the place.
senses.whyCN: 一个必须强硬才能活下来的地方也被称作 tough，人的品质被移到了地方上。

senses.title: A rough person
senses.definition: in informal use, a violent person or, admiringly, a strong one
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指凶暴的人，或带钦佩地指硬汉
senses.example: A few toughs were hanging around the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 几个混混在街角晃荡。
senses.why: The adjective is used as a noun, so a person with the quality comes to be named by it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词被当作名词用，于是具有这种品质的人就被它命名。

senses.title: To endure to the end
senses.definition: in informal use, to keep going through something hard, especially with out
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示在难事里坚持到底，尤与 out 连用
senses.example: The team had to tough it out until the storm passed.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍只得硬撑着等风暴过去。
senses.why: The verb turns strength into action: to stay firm until the difficulty is over.
senses.whyCN: 动词把强韧变成动作：一直挺住直到难事过去。

intro.en: Tough is an Old English adjective of strength, related to the verb for pulling, and its many figurative senses all rest on the idea of something that does not give way.
intro.cn: tough 是古英语中表示强韧的形容词，与「拉」的动词同源，其众多引申义都建立在「不肯屈服」这一想法上。

items.en: Toh describes what is strong and firm, and it is used of wood, leather, and rope.
items.cn: 古英语 toh 描述坚固结实之物，用于木、皮与绳索。

items.en: The stem is related to Old Norse tog, a rope or a pull, so strength and pulling belong together.
items.cn: 这个词干与古诺斯语 tog（绳、拉扯）相关，强韧与拉扯本是一体。

items.en: Middle English extends the word to food that resists the teeth and to people who resist hardship.
items.cn: 中古英语把该词扩展到抗齿的食物，也用于抗得住苦难的人。

items.en: The sense of a difficult task or a hard time appears and becomes the dominant everyday use.
items.cn: 「难办的事、艰难时期」义出现，并成为日常最主要的用法。

items.en: American English develops the admiring use of tough for a strong, unshakable person.
items.cn: 美式英语发展出带钦佩意味的 tough，指坚强不可动摇的人。

items.en: The casual verb to tough it out spreads in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 口语动词 tough it out 在二十世纪流行开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms with the same spelling pattern, while the near-meaning group gathers words for strength and for difficulty.
note.cn: 形近组收集拼写相近的形式，近义组则汇集表示强韧与困难的词。

entries.definition: the quality of being strong or severe
to make stronger or firmer
a difficult problem or person
despite the fact that
entries.definitionCN: 虽然，只是拼写相近，读音与词源不同

entries.definition: having great physical power
lasting a long time without damage
firm to the touch, or difficult
easily broken or damaged

normalIntro.en: These memories use the common collocations with time and decision, the verb pattern with out, and the comparison with though, a common spelling trap.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用 time、decision 等常见搭配、与 out 搭配的动词用法，以及与 though 的拼写对照。

normal.en: Tough rhymes with rough and enough, not with though.
normal.cn: tough 与 rough、enough 押韵，不与 though 同韵。

normal.en: A tough decision is hard, not strong; the context tells you which sense is meant.
normal.cn: a tough decision 指难，而非结实，语境决定义项。

normal.en: Tough it out means to endure until the end, and out signals the full stretch.
normal.cn: tough it out 指撑到最后，out 表示贯穿到底。

normal.en: Toughen adds -en to make a verb, as in toughen the rules.
normal.cn: toughen 加 -en 构成动词，如 toughen the rules。

normal.en: A tough act to follow means a hard standard to match, not a violent one.
normal.cn: a tough act to follow 指难以企及的标准，不是凶暴。

abstract.en: Picture a strap drawn tight, its surface lined but whole.
abstract.cn: 想象一条拉紧的皮带，表面起纹却完好无损。

abstract.en: Think of a year with nothing easy in it, walked through one day at a time.
abstract.cn: 想那一年没有一件容易事，却一天天走了过来。

abstract.en: What does not break under force becomes the word for what does not give up.
abstract.cn: 受力不断的东西，最终成了「不放弃」的那个词。

examples.en: These boots are tough enough for a week in the hills.
examples.cn: 这双靴子结实得够在山里走一星期。

examples.en: Leaving the job was a tough decision to make.
examples.cn: 辞掉这份工作是个艰难的决定。

examples.en: The government is getting tough on false advertising.
examples.cn: 政府在虚假广告问题上正变得强硬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塔夫」——塔夫绸又厚又耐磨，正像 tough 的坚韧。

root: 古英语 toh（坚韧），与古诺斯语 tog（绳、拉扯）同源。由「抗拉不断」引申出「难嚼、艰难、强硬、凶悍」，形容词又用作名词指硬汉。

sensesIntro.en: The entry starts from a material that will not break, then follows the same resistance into food, into hard times and hard tasks, into firm policy and rough manners, and finally into the noun and the casual verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从不会断裂的材料写起，再沿同一份「抵住」的力量走入食物、艰难的日子与难办的事，再进入强硬政策与凶悍作风，最后是名词与口语动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something that will not give way.
core.cn: 核心意象：不肯屈服之物。

branches.en: Material strength and food that resists the teeth.
branches.cn: 材料之强与抗齿之韧。

branches.en: Hard times and hard tasks.
branches.cn: 艰难时期与难办的事。

branches.en: Firm policy and rough surroundings.
branches.cn: 强硬的政策与凶悍的环境。

branches.en: The rough person named by the adjective.
branches.cn: 由形容词命名的凶悍之人。

branches.en: Enduring to the end.
branches.cn: 坚持到底。

intro.en: The word is a short inherited adjective whose family grows with -ness, -ly, -en, and -ie.
intro.cn: 本词是简短的继承形容词，其词族靠 -ness、-ly、-en 与 -ie 扩展。

latinIntro.en: This is a native word with no Latin ancestor, so the Latin entries give related words for strength.
latinIntro.cn: 本词是本土词，没有拉丁语祖先，故拉丁词条列出与强韧相关的词。

items.example: The stem is unchanged in spelling since Middle English.
items.exampleCN: 拼写自中古英语以来未变。

items.example: Toh is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: toh 是现存最早的记录形式。

items.example: The stem links strength with pulling.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干把强韧与拉扯连在一起。

items.example: Toughness is the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: toughness 是这种性质本身。

items.example: Toughly means in a firm way.
items.exampleCN: toughly 意为强硬地。

items.example: Toughen means to make tough.
items.exampleCN: toughen 意为使变坚韧。

items.meaning: a person or thing of a kind
items.example: A toughie is a hard problem.
items.exampleCN: toughie 是难题。

items.example: Tougher is the comparative form.
items.exampleCN: tougher 是比较级。

items.example: Toughest is the superlative form.
items.exampleCN: toughest 是最高级。

definition_zh: 旅行；参观；巡回演出；任职期；游览；巡回
definition_en: a journey in which several places are visited, or a period of duty in one place, or to travel around an area
core_image: 一辆大巴绕过广场，游客的目光顺着窗外的环形路线转了一圈
scene: 天刚亮，旅店门口就停下一辆白色大巴，导游举着小旗。We took a guided tour of the old town and finished at the harbour.
sceneCN: 这里 tour 是名词「游览、参观」（第 2 个义项：由导游带领的短程参观）；句意为我们跟着导游游览了老城，最后在港口结束。画面里有清晨的大巴、小旗与老城的石街。

pos.zh: 名词：旅行；游览；巡回演出；任期
动词：旅行；巡回（演出、访问）

derivatives.zh: 加 -ism 构成，义为「旅游业」
加 -ist 构成，义为「旅游者；游客」
加 -ing 构成，义为「巡回的；用于旅行的」
加前缀 de- 构成，义为「绕道；弯路」

senses.title: A journey through places
senses.definition: a journey visiting several places one after another
senses.definitionCN: 依次造访若干地方的旅行
senses.example: The band spent two years on a world tour.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队花了两年时间做世界巡演。
senses.why: The Latin and French word for a turn gives the idea of going round a set of places and returning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语与法语中表示「转」的词带来了绕行一圈再回来的概念。

senses.title: A short visit with a guide
senses.definition: a short organised visit to a place, often with a guide
senses.definitionCN: 由人带领下对某处的短程参观
senses.example: The guided tour lasts about an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这次有导游的参观大约一小时。
senses.why: A short circuit of a building or a town is a mini version of a long journey, so the same word serves.
senses.whyCN: 绕建筑或城镇走一圈是长途旅行的缩小版，于是同一个词也就够用了。

senses.title: A series of performances
senses.definition: a series of public performances or appearances in different places
senses.definitionCN: 在不同地点连续进行的演出或露面
senses.example: The play goes on tour in the autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这部戏秋天开始巡回上演。
senses.why: Performers who travel from town to town follow a circuit, which is exactly a tour.
senses.whyCN: 艺人逐城而行正是走一条环线，那恰好就是 tour。

senses.title: A period of duty abroad
senses.definition: a fixed period of service in one place, especially abroad or in the army
senses.definitionCN: 在某地（尤指海外或军中）的一段固定服役期
senses.example: He completed a two-year tour in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 他在北方完成了两年任期。
senses.why: A period assigned in one post resembles a round of duty that ends and returns, and soldiers borrowed the word for it.
senses.whyCN: 派在一处的一段时期像一趟有始有终的差事，军人便借用了这个词。

senses.title: To travel around
senses.definition: to travel through an area or a country, visiting several places
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地区或国家往来游览多处
senses.example: They toured the coast by train last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 去年夏天他们坐火车游了沿海一带。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb of going round, with the same image of a circle of visits.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为表示绕行的动词，仍是同一圈造访的意象。

senses.title: To take a visitor round
senses.definition: to show a person or a group round a place
senses.definitionCN: 带某人或某团体参观某处
senses.example: An old student toured us round the laboratories.
senses.exampleCN: 一位老学生带我们参观了实验室。
senses.why: Showing someone round is performing a tour for them, so the verb takes a person or a place as its object.
senses.whyCN: 带人参观就是替人做一趟 tour，故动词可接人或地方作宾语。

senses.title: On the road with a show
senses.definition: to go from place to place giving performances or making appearances
senses.definitionCN: 四处奔走演出或露面
senses.example: The singer toured Europe with a small band.
senses.exampleCN: 那位歌手带着一支小乐队巡演欧洲。
senses.why: This use fixes the word in the entertainment world, where the circuit of cities is a regular route.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法把词固定在演艺界，那里城市之间连成固定线路。

senses.title: A turn in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, a turn or a circular movement
senses.definitionCN: 较早文本中表示一转或环形运动
senses.example: The old clock's tour of the dial took a full day.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧钟的指针绕表盘一周要一整天。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a turn, and every later sense is a journey that comes back to its start.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是「一转」，后来所有义项都是回到起点的行程。

intro.en: Tour goes back to Latin tornare, to turn on a lathe, and through Old French tour, a turn, to the modern sense of a circular journey.
intro.cn: tour 可上溯到拉丁语 tornare（在车床上转），经古法语 tour（一转）而到现代表示环行旅程的意思。

items.en: Tornare means to turn or to make round, and tornus names a lathe.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tornare 意为转动、使成圆形，tornus 指车床。

items.en: Tornus itself comes from Greek tornos, a tool for drawing circles.
items.cn: tornus 本身来自希腊语 tornos，一种画圆的工具。

items.en: Old French tour means a turn, a circuit, or a round of duty.
items.cn: 古法语 tour 意为回转、一圈或一轮差事。

items.en: Middle English borrows tour for a journey that goes round and returns.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 tour，指绕行一圈再回来的行程。

items.en: The performing tour appears in the eighteenth century as companies travel between towns.
items.cn: 巡回演出之义于十八世纪出现，因为剧团在城镇间往来。

items.en: Tourism and tourist are coined in the early nineteenth century from the same stem.
items.cn: tourism 与 tourist 于十九世纪初由同一词干造出。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for journeys and visits.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干上的词，近义组则汇集表示旅行与参观的词。

entries.definition: a person travelling for pleasure
the business of holidays and travel
a longer way round
a tall narrow building
entries.definitionCN: 塔，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an act of travelling from one place to another
a short visit to a place and back
a short group journey for pleasure
a long journey by sea or in space

normalIntro.en: These memories use the fixed phrases on tour and a tour of, the compounds with guide and package, and the way the word marks a circle.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用 on tour 与 a tour of 的固定搭配、与 guide、package 构成的复合词，以及这个词的「一圈」意味。

normal.en: On tour describes a performer or a team, while on a tour describes a traveller.
normal.cn: on tour 指艺人或球队，on a tour 指旅行者。

normal.en: Tour guide and tour operator both put tour before the noun it describes.
normal.cn: tour guide 与 tour operator 都把 tour 放在所修饰名词之前。

normal.en: A package tour bundles travel, hotel, and food into one price.
normal.cn: a package tour 把交通、住宿与餐食打包成一个价钱。

normal.en: Tourist and tourism add -ist and -ism to the same stem.
normal.cn: tourist 与 tourism 是同一词干加 -ist 与 -ism。

normal.en: Detour takes the prefix de- and means a turn away from the direct road.
normal.cn: detour 加前缀 de-，意为偏离直路的绕行。

abstract.en: Picture a bus circling a square and coming back to the same corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆大巴绕广场一圈，又回到同一个街角。

abstract.en: Think of a clock hand sweeping the whole dial and ending where it began.
abstract.cn: 想钟表的指针扫过整个表盘，最后回到起点。

abstract.en: A tour is a turn made large: the same returning shape, drawn across places instead of minutes.
abstract.cn: 旅行是放大的「一转」：同样的回环之形，只是画在地点上而非时间上。

examples.en: The orchestra is on tour in Asia for six weeks.
examples.cn: 乐团正在亚洲巡演六周。

examples.en: She gave us a tour of the new library.
examples.cn: 她带我们参观了新图书馆。

examples.en: We toured the island by bicycle in four days.
examples.cn: 我们用四天骑自行车环游了这座岛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「图」——出门前先摊开一张地图，画个圈就是 tour。

root: 拉丁语 tornare（转）→ 拉丁语 tornus（车床）→ 古法语 tour（一转、一圈）→ 英语 tour。同族词有 tourist、tourism、detour；拉丁 tornare 亦生出 turn 与之同源。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the journey round several places, then reduces it to a short guided visit, widens it to a series of performances and to a term of duty, and closes with the verb and the old sense of a single turn.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从周游数地的旅程写起，再缩小为有导游的短程参观，扩大到巡回演出与海外任期，最后收在动词用法与「一转」这一古老义项上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of visits that returns to the start.
core.cn: 核心意象：绕行一圈又回到原处的造访。

branches.en: The long journey and the old sense of a turn.
branches.cn: 长途旅行与古老的「一转」义。

branches.en: A short guided visit and the act of showing round.
branches.cn: 短程参观与带人参观的动作。

branches.en: Concerts on the road and touring with a show.
branches.cn: 巡回演出与随团巡演。

branches.en: A fixed period of service abroad.
branches.cn: 海外的一段固定任期。

branches.en: Travelling around an area.
branches.cn: 在一地区内往来游览。

intro.en: The word is a short borrowed stem; its family comes from -ist, -ism, -ing, and the prefix de-.
intro.cn: 本词是简短的借入词干，其词族来自 -ist、-ism、-ing 与前缀 de-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the root of turning and the words built on it.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出「转」的词根及其构成的词。

items.example: The English form drops the final vowel sound.
items.exampleCN: 英语形式丢了末尾的元音。

items.example: Tornare is the ultimate source.
items.exampleCN: tornare 是最终来源。

items.example: Tornus gives the root image of turning.
items.exampleCN: tornus 给出「转」的核心意象。

items.example: A tourist travels for pleasure.
items.exampleCN: tourist 是为游乐而旅行的人。

items.example: Tourism is the trade of travel.
items.exampleCN: tourism 是旅行的行业。

items.example: Touring means travelling on a circuit.
items.exampleCN: touring 意为巡回的。

items.example: A detour turns away from the road.
items.exampleCN: detour 是从路上转开。

items.example: Toured is the past tense.
items.exampleCN: toured 是过去式。

items.example: Tours serves both uses.
items.exampleCN: tours 兼作两种用法。

definition_zh: 游客；旅游者；观光客
definition_en: a person who travels to a place for pleasure and stays there for a short time
core_image: 戴草帽的人举着相机站在老城广场中央，仰头看教堂尖顶
scene: 夏天的老城区，拖着行李箱的人在地图前停下来拍照。A tourist asked me which street led to the castle.
sceneCN: 这里 tourist 是「游客」（第 1 个义项：为游玩而到某地短暂停留的人）；句意为一位游客问我哪条街通往城堡。广场上举着相机仰头的人，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 观光客（贬义，指走马观花的人）

derivatives.zh: 由 tourist 换后缀 -ism 构成，义为「旅游业」
tourist 的词根，义为「旅行；游览」
由 tourist 加 -y 构成，义为「游客众多的；迎合游客的」

senses.title: The camera carrier
senses.definition: a person who visits a place for pleasure, often carrying a camera or a map
senses.definitionCN: 为游玩而到某地参观的人，常带着相机或地图
senses.example: A tourist asked me which street led to the castle.
senses.exampleCN: 一位游客问我哪条街通往城堡。
senses.why: The word names the role, not the person: anyone who travels for pleasure steps into it for a while.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一个角色而非某个人：任何为游玩而出行的人都会暂时走进这个角色。

senses.title: The shallow visitor
senses.definition: a slightly critical way of describing someone who sees only the famous sights of a place
senses.definitionCN: 略带批评地指只看一地著名景点、不求深入了解的人
senses.example: The old quarter is no longer a real neighbourhood, just a stop for tourists.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区已不再是真正的居民区，只是观光客的一站。
senses.why: Because a tourist often follows a guidebook, the word can carry the idea of seeing without understanding.
senses.whyCN: 因为游客常跟着导游手册走，这个词也带上了「看见却不理解」的意味。

senses.title: Trips made for visitors
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean connected with visitors and their travel
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示与游客及其出行有关的
senses.example: Tourist numbers rose sharply after the new airport opened.
senses.exampleCN: 新机场启用后游客人数大幅上升。
senses.why: The noun works as a label on things, so ticket, season and office can all wear the tourist tag.
senses.whyCN: 名词被拿来做标签贴在事物上，于是票、季节、办事处都能挂上 tourist 这个标签。

intro.en: Tourist is a modern English coinage built on tour, a word that came through French from Latin and Greek roots meaning a turning circle.
intro.cn: tourist 是近代英语在 tour 基础上造出的词，而 tour 经由法语来自拉丁语与希腊语中表示「转圈」的词根。

items.en: The noun tornos named a lathe, a tool that turns a piece of wood in a circle.
items.cn: 希腊语名词 tornos 指车床，即让木料转圈的工具。

items.en: From tornos came tornare, to turn, and then the noun tornus, a turn or a circuit.
items.cn: 由 tornos 生出动词 tornare（转），再有名词 tornus（一圈、一次周游）。

items.en: Old French made tour, a turn or a circular journey that ends where it began.
items.cn: 古法语造出 tour，指一次转身或绕行一周的旅程。

items.en: English borrowed tour, and an early tourist simply meant a person who makes a circular journey.
items.cn: 英语借入 tour，早期的 tourist 只表示作环行旅程的人。

items.en: With railways and holidays the meaning settled on the person who travels for pleasure.
items.cn: 随着铁路与假日的出现，词义固定为为游玩而出行的人。

note.en: The first group collects forms built on the same stem, the second collects other words for people who travel.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干构成的词，第二组收其他表示出行者的词。

entries.definition: The business of providing holidays for tourists.
A journey that visits several places.
Full of tourists or made for them.
A person who is on a journey.
A person who comes to see a place or a person.
A person who goes to see famous places.

normalIntro.en: Tourist is tour plus the person ending -ist, so the word literally means one who tours.
normalIntro.cn: tourist 就是 tour 加上表示人的后缀 -ist，字面意思即「绕行游览的人」。

normal.en: -ist marks the person who does the action of the stem.
normal.cn: -ist 标记执行词干动作的人。

normal.en: Tour means a circular journey, so a tourist goes round the sights.
normal.cn: tour 意为环行旅程，所以 tourist 就是绕景点走一圈的人。

normal.en: Tourism names the whole industry, tourist names one customer.
normal.cn: tourism 指整个行业，tourist 指一位顾客。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable, as in tourism.
normal.cn: 重音落在第一个音节，和 tourism 一样。

normal.en: A guidebook is written for the tourist, not by one.
normal.cn: 导游手册是写给游客的，而不是游客写的。

abstract.en: A camera raised above a crowd of heads.
abstract.cn: 人群中高举过头顶的一台相机。

abstract.en: A paper map folded until it fits one hand.
abstract.cn: 折到刚好一手能握住的一张纸质地图。

abstract.en: A suitcase wheel rattling over cobblestones.
abstract.cn: 行李箱轮子碾过石板路的响声。

examples.en: Tourists filled the square from morning until dark.
examples.cn: 游客从早到晚挤满了广场。

examples.en: Every tourist wants a photograph of the bridge at sunset.
examples.cn: 每位游客都想拍到日落时的桥。

examples.en: The town makes most of its money from tourism in summer.
examples.cn: 这个镇夏天大部分收入来自旅游业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拓瑞斯特」——拓下瑞丽的风景，斯特外地来的客，都是游客。

root: 由 tour（旅行，源自拉丁语 tornare 转、希腊语 tornos 车床）加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，字面即「作环行游览的人」，同族词有 tourism、touristy。

sensesIntro.en: First the person who travels for pleasure, then the shallow sightseer, then the adjective describing things made for them.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是为游玩而出行的人，再是走马观花的观光客，最后是修饰旅游事物的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a camera lifted above a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群中高举的相机。

branches.en: The person branch: one who travels for pleasure.
branches.cn: 人分支：为游玩而旅行的人。

branches.en: The judgement branch: one who sees without understanding.
branches.cn: 评价分支：只看而不理解的人。

branches.en: The label branch: things made for such people.
branches.cn: 标签分支：为这类人准备的事物。

branches.en: The street branch: cameras and crowds on the same avenue.
branches.cn: 街道分支：同一条大街上既有相机也有人群。

branches.en: The economy branch: visitors become an industry.
branches.cn: 经济分支：来访者变成一门产业。

intro.en: Tourist is built from the free stem tour plus the agent suffix -ist, and the family grows with -ism and -y.
intro.cn: tourist 由自由词干 tour 加施动后缀 -ist 构成，词族再靠 -ism、-y 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source tornare, to turn, also yields words about turning in circles, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源 tornare（转）还生出若干表示转圈的词，列在下面。

items.example: The stem names the journey itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名旅程本身。

items.example: It forms tourist, one who tours.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tourist，即游览的人。

items.example: It forms tourism, the activity of touring.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tourism，即旅游这项活动。

items.example: It forms touristy, full of tourists.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 touristy，游客味浓的。

items.example: The tourist bought a ticket.
items.exampleCN: 那位游客买了一张票。

items.meaningCN: 不止一位这样的旅行者
items.example: Tourists arrived by coach.
items.exampleCN: 游客乘大巴而来。

items.example: The old root also gives the turning rounds of a contest.
items.exampleCN: 同一个古老词根也生出比赛中一轮轮的周转。

items.example: The Latin root survives in this everyday verb.
items.exampleCN: 那个拉丁词根留在这个日常动词里。

definition_zh: 有毒的；毒性的；由毒物引起的；比喻有害的
definition_en: poisonous to living organisms, or harmful in a way compared to poison
core_image: 水边一只死鸟旁，黑色油泥泛着彩光，沾在手套上久久不散
scene: 志愿者在水边捡起一只死鸟，手套上沾着发亮的黑色油泥。The spill left a toxic residue along the shoreline.
sceneCN: 这里 toxic 指「对生物有毒的、能造成伤害的」（第 1 个义项：物质对活体生物具有毒性）；句意为泄漏在岸线上留下一层有毒残留物。图中可辨识物件：死鸟、黑色油泥、手套、岸线。

derivatives.zh: 毒素（生物产生的毒物）
毒性；毒力
毒理学
毒理学家
解毒；去毒

senses.title: Poisonous to living organisms
senses.definition: capable of harming or killing an organism by chemical action
senses.definitionCN: 能通过化学作用伤害或杀死生物的
senses.example: The spill left a toxic residue along the shoreline.
senses.exampleCN: 泄漏在岸线上留下一层有毒残留物。
senses.why: The word began as the adjective of Greek toxikon, the poison smeared on arrows, so its core image is a substance that kills at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是希腊 toxikon 的形容词，指涂在箭上的毒，因此核心意象是「能在远处致死的物质」。

senses.title: Caused by poison, as a medical condition
senses.definition: describing an illness, dose or effect produced by a poison or drug
senses.definitionCN: 描述由毒物或药物引起的疾病、剂量或效应
senses.example: The patient showed a toxic reaction to the drug.
senses.exampleCN: 病人对该药出现了毒性反应。
senses.why: Medicine needed an adjective for harm caused by a substance, as distinct from harm caused by infection or injury.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个形容词来指「由物质造成的伤害」，以区别于感染或外伤造成的伤害。

senses.title: Chemically hazardous in industry
senses.definition: describing waste, gas or material that must be handled under special safety rules
senses.definitionCN: 描述必须在专门安全规则下处理的废物、气体或材料
senses.example: Toxic waste must be stored away from the water table.
senses.exampleCN: 有毒废物必须远离地下水位存放。
senses.why: Regulation turned the adjective into a label that triggers permits, protective gear and disposal rules.
senses.whyCN: 监管把这个形容词变成一个标签，一贴上就触发许可、防护装备与处置规则。

senses.title: Produced by a living organism
senses.definition: describing a poison made by a plant, animal or microbe, as in a toxic secretion
senses.definitionCN: 描述由植物、动物或微生物制造的毒物，如毒性分泌物
senses.example: The frog's skin carries a toxic secretion.
senses.exampleCN: 这只蛙的皮肤带有毒性分泌物。
senses.why: Biology separates what is made by life from what is made in a factory, though both are called toxic.
senses.whyCN: 生物学要区分「生命制造的」与「工厂制造的」，尽管两者都叫 toxic。

senses.title: Harmful to a person's mind or relationships
senses.titleCN: 对人的心理或关系有害的
senses.definition: describing behaviour, a relationship or an atmosphere that damages people psychologically
senses.definitionCN: 描述在心理上伤害人的行为、关系或氛围
senses.example: She left a toxic working environment.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开了一个有害的工作环境。
senses.why: The metaphor works because the harm is slow, cumulative and hard to see, like exposure to a poison.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，是因为伤害缓慢、累积且难以看见，像接触毒物一样。

senses.title: Worthless and dangerous financial assets
senses.definition: describing loans or securities whose value has collapsed and which threaten the holder
senses.definitionCN: 描述价值已崩塌、并危及持有者的贷款或证券
senses.example: The bank was left holding toxic assets.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行最后手里握着有毒资产。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the word because the asset poisons the balance sheet it sits on.
senses.whyCN: 金融界借用这个词，因为这类资产会毒害它所在的资产负债表。

senses.title: Slang: extremely bad or unpleasant
senses.titleCN: 口语：极糟的、令人难受的
senses.definition: an informal use meaning very bad, offensive or unbearable
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指很糟、令人反感或难以忍受
senses.example: The traffic was toxic all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午的交通都糟透了。
senses.why: Slang strips the word down to pure intensity, keeping the sense of harm without any chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 口语把这个词剥离成纯粹的强度，只留「有害」的感觉，不带任何化学含义。

senses.title: Listed as toxic by regulation
senses.definition: formally classified as a hazardous substance with a defined threshold and reporting duty
senses.definitionCN: 被正式归为危险物质，附有明确阈值与申报义务
senses.example: The solvent is toxic under the clean-air rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这种溶剂在清洁空气法规下被列为有毒。
senses.why: A legal label is a separate sense because the classification does not depend on how the substance behaves in each case.
senses.whyCN: 法律标签之所以是独立义项，是因为归类并不取决于该物质在每种情形下的实际表现。

senses.title: Abstract: corrosive to a group or culture
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：对群体或文化起腐蚀作用
senses.definition: describing norms, speech or incentives that slowly damage trust and cooperation
senses.definitionCN: 描述缓慢损害信任与合作的规范、言论或激励机制
senses.example: The report called the incentives toxic for new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称这些激励机制对新员工有害。
senses.why: The final extension keeps the medical shape: a small repeated exposure produces a systemic illness.
senses.whyCN: 最后的延伸保留了医学形态：少量而反复的接触会造成全身性的病症。

intro.en: Toxic came to English through Latin from Greek, where the original poison was the one put on arrows. The figurative senses are modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: toxic 经拉丁语从希腊语进入英语，原本的毒是涂在箭上的那种。比喻义是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Toxon meant 'bow'. Its own origin is uncertain; it is often treated as a borrowing from a non-Greek language, so any older form offered for it is a hypothesis rather than a proved source.
items.cn: toxon 意为「弓」。它本身的来源不确定；常被看作借自某种非希腊语，因此凡为它给出的更早形式都是假说，而非已证实的来源。

items.en: Toxikon (pharmakon) meant 'arrow poison', literally the thing of the bow; the adjective toxikos described what belonged to the bow or to its poison.
items.cn: toxikon（pharmakon）意为「箭毒」，字面是「属于弓的东西」；形容词 toxikos 描述属于弓或其毒物者。

items.en: Latin toxicum meant 'poison', and toxicus was its adjective; medieval and early modern writers used both for venoms and drugs.
items.cn: 拉丁 toxicum 意为「毒」，toxicus 是其形容词；中世纪与近代早期作者用两者兼指毒液与药物。

items.en: English toxic appears in the seventeenth century as a learned adjective meaning 'poisonous', alongside the noun toxicum.
items.cn: 英语 toxic 在十七世纪作为学术形容词出现，意为「有毒的」，同时还有名词 toxicum。

items.en: Toxicology and industrial hygiene made toxic a standard term for chemical harm, and twentieth-century law turned it into a regulatory category.
items.cn: 毒理学与工业卫生使 toxic 成为化学危害的标准术语，二十世纪的法律又把它变成监管类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin of toxon, first date of the figurative senses): the bow word may be a foreign borrowing whose source is unknown, and no single earliest citation is fixed for the relational or slang senses, so their dates are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（toxon 的来源、比喻义的首见年代）：「弓」这个词可能是外来借词，而借自何处不明；关系义与口语义也没有公认的最早书证，年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same poison stock that differ in part of speech or in sense; group two holds adjectives of harm, each with its own route of injury.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「毒」词干、词性或含义不同的词；第二组是表示「有害」的形容词，各自的伤害路径不同。

entries.definition: A poison made by a living organism, such as a bacterial toxin; toxic is the adjective describing such a substance or its effect.
entries.definitionCN: 由活生物制造的毒物，如细菌毒素；toxic 是描述这种物质或其效应的形容词。

entries.definition: The study of poisons and their effects; it is a discipline name, not a description of a substance.
entries.definitionCN: 研究毒物及其效应的学科；它是学科名称，而非物质描述。

entries.definition: To make drunk or wildly excited, from the same toxicum; the modern sense has left poison behind.
entries.definitionCN: 使醉或使极度兴奋，同出 toxicum；现代义已离开了「毒」的意思。

entries.definition: A condition in which toxins are present in the blood; it names the medical state rather than the property.
entries.definitionCN: 毒素存在于血液中的状况；它命名的是医学状态，而非性质。

entries.definition: Able to harm when eaten, drunk or touched; it is the everyday word, while toxic is the technical and figurative one.
entries.definitionCN: 吃下、喝下或接触时能造成伤害；它是日常词，而 toxic 更技术化、也更多比喻用法。

entries.definition: Able to inject poison through a bite or sting; a venomous animal is not simply toxic, because the delivery matters.
entries.definitionCN: 能通过咬或蜇注入毒液；venomous 的动物不能简单说成 toxic，因为「如何送入」很关键。

entries.definition: Harmful, especially to health or to the senses, as of fumes; it stresses the unpleasant exposure rather than the chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 有害的，尤指对健康或感官，如烟气；它强调难受的接触，而非化学性质。

entries.definition: Extremely infectious or severe, used of pathogens and, figuratively, of hostility; it is about spreading power, not poison.
entries.definitionCN: 传染性极强或极严重的，用于病原体，也比喻敌意；它讲的是传播力，而非毒性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is Greek toxon 'bow': the first toxic thing was arrow poison.
normal.cn: 词根是希腊 toxon「弓」：最早的「有毒之物」是箭毒。

normal.en: The family runs toxin, toxicity, toxicology, toxicologist and detoxify.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 toxin、toxicity、toxicology、toxicologist 与 detoxify。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: toxic waste, toxic substance, toxic effect, highly toxic.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：有毒废物、有毒物质、毒性效应、剧毒的。

normal.en: Toxic is the adjective; toxin is the substance; toxicity is the degree.
normal.cn: toxic 是形容词；toxin 是物质；toxicity 是程度。

normal.en: Venomous means injected by bite or sting, which is narrower than toxic.
normal.cn: venomous 指经咬或蜇注入，比 toxic 窄。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of poison that takes hours to show its work.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴毒物要过几个小时才显出作用。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every conversation leaves you a little more tired.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，每次谈话都让你更疲惫一点。

abstract.en: Picture a loan on a ledger that quietly poisons every page around it.
abstract.cn: 想象账本上的一笔贷款，悄悄毒害周围每一页。

examples.en: The compound is toxic to fish at very low concentrations.
examples.cn: 这种化合物在极低浓度下就对鱼类有毒。

examples.en: Workers handling toxic waste wear sealed suits.
examples.cn: 处理有毒废物的工人穿着密封防护服。

examples.en: The label toxic is also used for relationships and cultures.
examples.cn: toxic 这个标签也被用于关系和职场文化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「tox（弓/箭）+ ic」——涂在箭上的那种东西 → 有毒的

root: 拉丁 toxicus < toxicum「毒」< 希腊 toxikon（pharmakon）「箭毒」< toxon「弓」；toxon 的来源不确定，可能借自非希腊语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one poison: the substance, the dose, the body, the damage, the label, and then relationships, money, slang and culture borrow the same shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一种毒展开：物质、剂量、身体、损害、标签，随后关系、金钱、口语与文化都借用了同一形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: arrow poison, a substance that kills from a distance.
core.cn: 核心意象：箭毒，一种能在远处致死的物质。

branches.en: BODY: the property of poison and the medical reaction are the same harm seen from outside and inside.
branches.cn: 身体：毒的性质与医学反应，是同一伤害从外面与里面看到的样子。

branches.en: LABEL: industrial handling and legal classification both turn toxicity into a rule.
branches.cn: 标签：工业处置与法律归类都把毒性变成一条规则。

branches.en: LIFE-MADE: a secretion from a plant or animal is poison with a maker.
branches.cn: 生物制造：植物或动物的分泌物，是有制造者的毒。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND FINANCIAL: a relationship and a bad loan both poison what contains them.
branches.cn: 社会与金融：一段关系与一笔坏账，都会毒害容纳它们的东西。

branches.en: INTENSITY: slang keeps only the harm, and culture keeps the slow cumulative exposure.
branches.cn: 强度：口语只留下「有害」，文化义保留「缓慢累积的接触」。

intro.en: Toxic is a Greek-derived adjective with a root that reaches back to the bow and a suffix that makes a quality.
intro.cn: toxic 是希腊来源形容词，词根可追到「弓」，后缀则构成性质形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin toxicum gives toxic, toxin, toxicity, toxicology and intoxicate; Greek toxon 'bow' is the root behind all of them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 toxicum 衍生 toxic、toxin、toxicity、toxicology 与 intoxicate；希腊 toxon「弓」是它们共同的根。

items.example: The bow word gave its name to arrow poison.
items.exampleCN: 「弓」这个词把名字给了箭毒。

items.structure: toxikon (Greek adjective/noun, 'of the bow; arrow poison')
items.example: Toxikon named the poison on the arrowhead.
items.exampleCN: toxikon 指涂在箭头上的毒。

items.example: The adjective entered English as toxic.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词以 toxic 进入英语。

items.example: The suffix makes a quality adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成性质形容词。

items.example: The gas was toxic in the tunnel.
items.exampleCN: 隧道里的气体有毒。

items.meaning: a poison, especially from an organism
items.example: The bacterium released a toxin.
items.exampleCN: 细菌释放出一种毒素。

items.example: They measured the toxicity of the sample.
items.exampleCN: 他们测定了样本的毒性。

items.example: Toxicology screened the water.
items.exampleCN: 毒理学对水做了筛查。

items.example: The liver detoxifies the blood.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏为血液解毒。

items.example: The drink intoxicated him quickly.
items.exampleCN: 这酒很快让他醉了。

definition_zh: 痕迹；踪迹；微量；（作动词）追溯；追踪；描摹
definition_en: a mark or sign left by something that has passed, or to follow such marks back to their source
core_image: 泥地上的一串脚印，一直延伸到树林里
scene: 雨后的田埂上留着一行野兽的脚印，猎狗低头嗅着，一步一步往里走。The hunters followed the trace of a deer to the edge of the marsh.
sceneCN: 这里 trace 是「踪迹、痕迹」（第 1 个义项：某物经过后留下的印记）；句意为猎人循着鹿的踪迹一直走到了沼泽边缘。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「描摹；追踪；描图纸」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「追踪者；示踪剂」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可追溯的」

senses.title: A mark left behind by movement
senses.definition: a sign such as footprints, a line, or a stain left by something moving or present
senses.definitionCN: 由物体移动或出现而留下的脚印、线条或污渍等记号
senses.example: There were fresh traces of mud on the kitchen floor.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房地板上留下了新鲜的泥痕。
senses.why: The Latin source is a verb of drawing a line, so a trace is what a passing line leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源是「画线」的动词，所以痕迹就是一条经过的线所留下的东西。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a tiny quantity of something, especially one barely detectable
senses.definitionCN: 极少的量，尤指几乎难以察觉的一点
senses.example: The water showed traces of copper from the old pipes.
senses.exampleCN: 水里检出了老管道带来的一丝铜。
senses.why: If only a mark remains of something, then only a little of it is left, and that little becomes the second sense.
senses.whyCN: 若某物只剩下一个印记，那就只剩一点点，而这一点点便成了第二个义项。

senses.title: To follow marks to their source
senses.definition: to find the origin or history of something by following the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 循着证据找出某物的起源或来历
senses.example: Scholars traced the proverb back to a Latin writer.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们把这句谚语追溯到一位拉丁作家。
senses.why: Following a line drawn by something is following its path backwards, which is what tracing an origin means.
senses.whyCN: 顺着某物画出的线走，就是反向跟随它的路径，这正是「追溯起源」的意思。

senses.title: To copy a shape by drawing over it
senses.definition: to copy a picture by placing thin paper over it and drawing the lines
senses.definitionCN: 把薄纸覆在图上，照着线条描出图形
senses.example: She traced the outline of the leaf onto the page.
senses.exampleCN: 她把叶子的轮廓描到了纸上。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the Latin verb is to draw a line, and copying a shape is the most literal drawing of lines.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词最古老的含义就是画线，而照着轮廓画线是最字面的用法。

senses.title: To find the course of something
senses.definition: to follow the path or development of something step by step
senses.definitionCN: 一步一步跟随某物的路线或发展
senses.example: They traced the river from the mountains to the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从山间到大海沿途追查这条河。
senses.why: Once you have a line, you can walk along it, and the word moves from drawing a path to following one.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了一条线，就能顺着它走，于是这个词从「画路径」转到「跟随路径」。

intro.en: Trace comes from Old French tracier, from Latin tractus, a dragging or a drawing out, which is built on the verb trahere, to pull.
intro.cn: trace 来自古法语 tracier，源自拉丁语 tractus（拖、拉出），建立在动词 trahere（拉）之上。

items.en: Trahere means to pull or draw; its participle tractus means a dragging or a drawn line.
items.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 意为拉、拖；其分词 tractus 意为「拖拽」或「画出的线」。

items.en: Old French tracier means to draw a line, to mark out a path, or to make a sketch.
items.cn: 古法语 tracier 意为画线、标出路径或勾勒草图。

items.en: English borrows the word first for a mark on the ground left by a person or animal.
items.cn: 英语先借入这个词，指人或动物留在地上的印记。

items.en: In the seventeenth century the abstract sense of tracing a story or a family back to its origin develops.
items.cn: 十七世纪发展出「把一段经过或一个家族追溯到源头」的抽象含义。

items.en: The scientific use for tiny amounts, such as trace elements, becomes standard in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 表示极微量的科学用法（如微量元素）在十九、二十世纪成为标准。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin pulling root, while the near-meaning group gathers words for signs and for following a path.
note.cn: 形近组收集建立在拉丁语「拉」这一词根上的词，近义组收集表示记号与跟随路径的词。

entries.definition: a copy made by drawing over lines
something that follows or marks a course
a path or the marks left on it
entries.definitionCN: 轨道；足迹，拼写相近但来源不同

entries.definition: to pull something out
a visible sign on a surface
signs that show something is true
a mark left by a foot

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the pulling root, from the family with -ing, -er, and -able, and from the collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「拉」这个词根、由 -ing、-er、-able 构成的词族以及常用搭配入手。

normal.en: Trahere is to pull, so a trace is something drawn out along a line.
normal.cn: trahere 是拉，所以 trace 是沿着一条线拉出来的东西。

normal.en: Trace, tracing, tracer, traceable: noun, act, person, and possibility.
normal.cn: trace、tracing、tracer、traceable，分别是名词、行为、人、可能性。

normal.en: Trace back to is the key phrase: follow the line backwards until it starts.
normal.cn: trace back to 是关键搭配：沿着线往回走，直到它的起点。

normal.en: Without a trace means the line has disappeared completely.
normal.cn: without a trace 意味着这条线完全消失了。

normal.en: A trace of salt is a mark of salt left in the water, not the salt itself.
normal.cn: a trace of salt 是水里的盐留下的印记，而不是盐本身。

abstract.en: Picture a finger drawing a line in dust, then the line slowly being blown away.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在灰上画出一条线，然后线被慢慢吹散。

abstract.en: Think of a thin thread pulled out of a cloth, going back to the loom.
abstract.cn: 想一根从布里抽出的细线，一路回到织机。

abstract.en: A trace is the past still visible on a surface.
abstract.cn: 痕迹是仍然留在表面上的过去。

examples.en: The police found no trace of the missing boat.
examples.cn: 警方没有找到失踪船只的任何踪迹。

examples.en: The word traces back to an old French verb.
examples.cn: 这个词可以追溯到古法语的一个动词。

examples.en: There was a trace of anger in her voice.
examples.cn: 她的声音里有一丝怒意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「戳一斯」——在泥里戳一下，留下一条印子，就是痕迹。

root: 拉丁语 trahere（拉、拖）→ 分词 tractus（拉出的线）→ 古法语 tracier（画线）→ 中古英语 trace。同源词有 track、tract、extract、attract、contract。

sensesIntro.en: From the drawn line the entry spreads in two directions: backwards into the mark left behind and the tiny remains it implies, and forwards into drawing copies and following paths to an origin.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「画出的线」出发，本词向两个方向展开：向内是留下的印记以及由此而来的微量残余，向外是描摹与循路追到源头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line in the dust showing where something passed.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰土上的一条线，显示出某物经过的路线。

branches.en: The mark itself.
branches.cn: 印记本身。

branches.en: The little that the mark implies.
branches.cn: 印记所暗示的那一点残余。

branches.en: The line drawn by copying.
branches.cn: 照着描出的线。

branches.en: The line followed along a route.
branches.cn: 沿着路线跟随的线。

branches.en: The line followed back to its start.
branches.cn: 顺着线走回起点。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin stem tract- pulled into French and English, and its family is formed with -ing, -er, and -able.
intro.cn: 本词带着拉丁词干 tract- 经法语进入英语，其词族由 -ing、-er、-able 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb and its participle are the base of the whole English family, from trace to extract.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁动词及其分词是 trace 到 extract 整个英语词族的基础。

items.example: The stem appears in trace, track, and extract.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在 trace、track、extract 中。

items.example: Transport means to carry across.
items.exampleCN: transport 意为运过去。

items.example: Extract means to pull out.
items.exampleCN: extract 意为拉出。

items.example: Attract means to pull towards.
items.exampleCN: attract 意为拉向。

items.example: Contract means to pull together.
items.exampleCN: contract 意为拉紧收缩。

items.example: Tracing is the act and its product.
items.exampleCN: tracing 既是行为也是产物。

items.example: A tracer follows a course.
items.exampleCN: tracer 沿路追踪。

items.example: Traceable means it can be followed back.
items.exampleCN: traceable 意为可追溯的。

latinEntries.meaning: drawn; a drawing out, a course

definition_zh: 轨道；足迹；小径；跑道；（作动词）追踪；跟踪；记录
definition_en: a narrow path or railway line, or the marks left by movement, and to follow those marks or keep a record of something
core_image: 两道平行的铁轨在野草之间拐了个弯
scene: 荒废的支线上长满了草，只有两条铁轨还亮着，一直通向远处的山口。The old track runs behind the farm and disappears into the hills.
sceneCN: 这里 track 是「铁轨、轨道」（第 2 个义项：供火车行驶的两条钢轨）；句意为这条旧轨道从农舍后面延伸过去，消失在山间。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，义为「追踪者；追踪器」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「追踪；定位」
由 track 加 -less 构成，义为「无路的；无足迹的」

senses.title: A narrow path beaten by feet
senses.definition: a rough path in the countryside made by people or animals walking on it
senses.definitionCN: 乡间由人或动物反复行走踩出的小路
senses.example: A narrow track leads from the gate to the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 一条窄窄的小路从大门通到果园。
senses.why: The word comes from an old verb of drawing or dragging, and a path is literally a line drawn by walking.
senses.whyCN: 本词来自表示拉、拖的古老动词，而小路就是被走线一样「画」出来的。

senses.title: The pair of rails for a train
senses.definition: the steel lines on which a train runs
senses.definitionCN: 供火车行驶的两条钢轨
senses.example: The train slowed as it entered the single track.
senses.exampleCN: 火车进入单线轨道时慢了下来。
senses.why: Rails are the most fixed line of all, so the path sense hardens into the metal route of a railway.
senses.whyCN: 钢轨是最固定的一条线，于是小径之义硬化为铁路的金属路线。

senses.title: Marks left by a moving animal
senses.definition: the prints or signs left by an animal or person walking
senses.definitionCN: 动物或人走动时留下的印迹
senses.example: There were deer tracks in the fresh snow.
senses.exampleCN: 新雪上有鹿的足迹。
senses.why: A path is a line of steps, and the steps themselves leave marks, so both are called by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 小路是一串步子画出的线，而步子本身也留下印记，两者用同一个词表示。

senses.title: To follow a person or animal
senses.definition: to follow the movements of someone or something, often without being seen
senses.definitionCN: 跟随着某人或某物的行动，常常不被察觉
senses.example: They tracked the wolf for two days across the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在冰原上追踪那头狼两天。
senses.why: Reading a line of prints becomes the action of following it, so the noun turns into a verb.
senses.whyCN: 读懂一串脚印，就成了跟着这串脚印走，于是名词转为动词。

senses.title: To keep a record of something
senses.definition: to keep an up-to-date record of how a process, cost, or set of things is changing
senses.definitionCN: 持续记录某个过程、费用或事物集合的变化
senses.example: The app tracks my spending month by month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用按月记录我的支出。
senses.why: Keeping track of something is drawing its line as it happens, so recording becomes a kind of tracking.
senses.whyCN: keep track of 就是一边发生一边画出它的线，所以记录也是一种追踪。

senses.title: A prepared course for running
senses.definition: a running course marked out with lanes for sport
senses.definitionCN: 用分道标记出来的体育跑道
senses.example: The runners lined up on the track before the whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 哨响之前，跑者们在跑道上排好了队。
senses.why: A marked line drawn on the ground for a purpose is the most literal reading of the old drawing sense.
senses.whyCN: 为了某个目的在地上画出的标记线，正是古老「画线」语义最字面的读法。

intro.en: Track is borrowed from Old French trac, a trace or a trail, probably Germanic in final origin, and it is related to the Latin pulling root behind trace.
intro.cn: track 借自中古法语 trac（痕迹、行迹），更远来源大概是日耳曼语，并与 trace 背后拉丁语「拉」的词根有关。

items.en: The ultimate origin is probably a Germanic word for a mark drawn or dragged, though the details are debated.
items.cn: 其最终来源大概是日耳曼语中表示「拖出的记号」的词，细节尚有争议。

items.en: Old French trac means a trail, a mark of passage, and also the act of drawing a line.
items.cn: 古法语 trac 意为行迹、经过的记号，也指画线的动作。

items.en: English adopts track in the fifteenth century for a footprint or a path made by walking.
items.cn: 中古英语在十五世纪借入 track，指脚印或走出来的路。

items.en: When railways spread in the nineteenth century, the rails themselves are called the track.
items.cn: 十九世纪铁路普及后，钢轨本身就被称为 track。

items.en: The verb meaning to follow traces is old, but tracking in the modern sense of monitoring a process is recent.
items.cn: 表示跟随痕迹的动词用法很古老，但「监控过程」的现代追踪义是晚近的事。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same drawing and pulling root, while the near-meaning group gathers paths and signs of passage.
note.cn: 形近组收集建立在同一「画线、拉」词根上的词，近义组收集路径与经过的记号。
